For that he is also. In the word be-shaggam (for that also) the shin placed before gam (also) has the same meaning as the shin placed before kakhah (thus). The term My spirit refers to Elokim’s spirit, for man’s spirit comes from Elokim. Similarly, And the spirit returneth unto Elokim who gave it (Kohelet 12:7). The spirit spoken of by Ecclesiastes refers only to the spirit in man. The meaning of the verse is: My spirit shall not abide in man because of his violent ways and because he is (be-shaggem) made of flesh, grows until he achieves maturity, and then due to his sexual activity begins his decline.

Therefore shall his days be a hundred and twenty years. Some explain that this refers to man’s life span. If we find some living longer than this, they are but a few. Our verse speaks of most people. However, this interpretation is not correct. Behold, Shem lived for six hundred years. Also, the generations that followed him lived many, many years beyond a hundred and twenty. It was only in the days of Peleg (Bereshit 10:25) that the life span was shortened. From the days of King David onward it has been limited to seventy or eighty years. The correct meaning of therefore shall his days be a hundred and twenty years is as Onkelos explained, namely, that Hashem set a time for mankind to repent. We see the same idea in Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown (Yonah 3:4). Hashem gave them one hundred and twenty years in which to repent and save themselves, or to remain unrepentant and perish. Scripture’s statement, And Noach was five hundred years old, and Noach begot Shem, Cham and Yefet (Bereshit 5:32), should not disturb you, because the Bible is not in chronological sequence. Note, the Torah states, and Terach died in Charan (Bereshit 11:32), then goes on to say, Now Hashem said unto Avram: Get thee out of thy country (Bereshit 12:1). However, we know that Terach did not die until Yitzchak was thirty-five years old. There are many other similar instances in Scripture.
[The nephilim.] They were so named because anyone who saw them lost heart at their huge stature.
[After that.] After the flood. Behold, the sons of Anak (Bamidbar 13:33) were originally from the family of the sons of Elokim.

And it repented Hashem. The Torah spoke in the language of men, for we know that Hashem is not a man that he should repent. This term is used because if a human being acted in the way Hashem did, destroying his creation, it would be said of him that he repented.

[And it grieved him at his heart.] This verse is the opposite of Let Hashem rejoice in His works (Tehillim 104:31). Hashem is said to be happy when his creatures benefit from his acts of kindness. Others say that va-yinnachem (and it repented) should be rendered as set a time, as in doth comfort (mitnachem) himself, purposing to kill thee (Bereshit 27:42). They also say that His heart does not refer to the heart of Hashem but to the heart of the prophet. However, if this were the case Scripture should not have read: and it grieved “at” (el) His heart. Secondly, where do we find a prophet called a heart?
And the Lord said. In His heart, or to the angels; others say, to Noach. However, it appears to me that And the Lord said is connected to His heart of the previous verse.

Grace. Chen (grace) means mercy. From it we get the word techinnah (supplication). Chen follows the paradigm of ketz (end); both have roots whose second and third letters are the same. The meaning of found grace (mercy or pity) in the eyes of the Lord is like No eye pitied thee (Yechezkel 16:5).

These are the generations. Toledot (generations) means the events that transpired during his lifetime, as in what a day may bring forth (yeled) (Mishlei 27:1). These are the generations of Yaakov (Bereshit 37:2) is similar.
A man righteous. In his deeds.
And whole-hearted. In his heart. Tamim (wholehearted) is an adjective. It belongs to those roots whose second and third letters are the same. All three letters of the root remain in this word.

[In his generations.] At the time of the flood, and in the generations after the flood. For Noach lived till the fifty-eighth year of Avraham. Let this be a mnemonic device, our father Avraham was the age of Noach (58) when Noach died.
And the earth was corrupt. The people of the earth were corrupt. Similarly, when a land sinneth against Me (Yechezkel 14:13), and And all countries came into Mitzrayim (Bereshit 41:57).

[Before God.] Some say this means they sinned in public. Others say it means people were privately corrupt with regard to secret affairs so that only God was aware of their sins. In my opinion, the Torah speaks the language of men so that people will understand what is being said. The meaning of before God is that they acted like a servant, who in the presence of his master, disobeys him and thereby shows that he does not fear him. Those who say that Elokim (God) does not refer to the Almighty are speaking nonsense.
Violence. Theft, oppression and taking women against their will.

Our sages are correct in interpreting for all flesh had corrupted their way to mean that all flesh engaged in unnatural and perverted sexual acts. Indeed, how precious is their interpretation to the effect that they corrupted with water and were punished by Hashem with water. Just as they placed their waters above and below, so Hashem punished them by a flood whose waters came from above and below.
And God said unto Noach: the end of all flesh. All bodies.
[Is come before me.] The time of their calamity has arrived.

With the earth. Et ha’aretz (with the earth) means from the earth. Similarly, As soon as I am gone out of the city (et ha’ir) (Shemot 9:29). It may also be rendered, with the earth, as in with Yaakov (et Yaakov) every man came with his household (Shemot 1:1). It appears to me that mashchitam (I will destroy them) stands for two words. Similarly, the word Elokim in O Elokim of hosts (Tehillim 80:8) and thy throne in thy throne Elokim (Tehillim 45:7). The meaning of our verse is: And, behold, I will destroy them and destroy the earth.
Gopher. Gopher is the name of a wood that rides lightly upon the water. It is mentioned nowhere else in Scripture.
Rooms. So that each animal, cattle and fowl would be alone with its mate.
[Ark.] The Bible uses the term ark and not ship, for it did not have the shape of a ship nor did it have oars.

And shalt pitch it. Some say that ve-khafarta (and shalt pitch) comes from the same root as kapporet (cover) (Shemot 25:17), the meaning of and shalt pitch it being you shall cover it by coating it. [PITCH.] Some say that kofer is a pitch-like substance. Others say that a certain clay with pitch-like qualities is found in the ground and is to be identified with the kofer in our verse. Others identify it with a substance similarly called in Arabic while noting that in Arabic it is spelled with a kof rather than a caf. In reality, ve-khafarta (and shalt pitch) is a denominative of kofer.
Within. On the inside.

And this is how thou shalt make it. These are the dimensions which you shall make it. Its height was a tenth of its length, so that it would be able to float on the water and not be overturned by the wind.

A light. Tzohar (a light) means an opening through which light would enter. It comes from the same root as tzohorayim (noon). The opening was made in the usual place, on top of the ark. Scripture tells us that the top of the ark was a cubit in length. We gather from this that it was a sixth of a cubit wide. The ark was triangular in shape. Its top came to a point, and so did its corners. Therefore it did not overturn. The door was on one side and was reached by climbing a ladder. Now, we know that the ark was very large. Furthermore, it is possible that Noach was much taller than we, for the cubits mentioned with regard to the ark are Noach’s cubits. It is also possible, since the ark was divided into three stories, that the bottom story was ten cubits high. Some say that the ark had many stories and that Scripture abridged the number.

Lower, second and third. These are all adjectives. Those who ask why shelishim (third) is not written selishiyyim have eyes but do not see. Can’t they see that forgiving, archer and thief are adjectives, as are prince, deputy, pious, wise and understanding? Nevertheless, each of these words is vocalized according to its own pattern and form. Shelishim (third) follows the paradigm of negidim (princes) and chasidim (pious). This is so because the singular of shelishim is shalish, as the singular of chasidim is chasid. It is also possible that the dagesh in the yod of sheniyyim (second) also applies to the yod of shelishim (third). Perhaps this will satisfy those who raised the question.

And I. Some say that the dagesh in mabbul (flood) is in place of a missing nun, as in the word mabbua (fountain). They note that the word mabbul comes from the same root as navelah (fadeth) in The earth fainteth and fadeth (navelah) away (Is. 24:4). Others say that mabbul comes from the same root as balul (mingled) in mingled (belulah) with oil, and that it should have followed the paradigm of maslul (highway) (Is. 35:8). The word massor (saw) (Is. 10:15) with a shuruk and a cholam interchanging is analogous.

[The flood of waters.] This is an abridged phrase. It should be read as follows: The flood, a flood of waters. Similarly the meaning of since the day it was founded (Shemot 9:18) is: since the day, the day it was founded.

But I will establish my covenant. This indicates, although not previously mentioned, that Hashem had sworn earlier to Noach that he and his children would not die in the flood. We find a similar instance in Deuteronomy, viz., Let us send men before us, that they may search the land for us (Devarim 1:22). But I will establish means I will keep my oath. However, it appears to me that the covenant alludes to the covenant that would be made at the time Hashem set the rainbow in the sky. Covenant means an agreement and a thing which two sides choose. It comes from the same root as beru (choose) in choose (beru) you a man for you (Shmuel I 17:8). The word for covenant (brit) has this form and vocalization both in the absolute and in the construct. We find the same thing with the word shevit (captivity). We thus read, Thou hast turned the captivity of Yaakov (shevit Yaakov) (Tehillim 85:2), and And his daughters into captivity (ba-shevit) (Bamidbar 21:29). Others say that a brit (covenant) is a cut boundary.

[Two of every sort.] After stating two, Scripture goes on to explain that this refers to male and female. After stating generally, And of every living thing of all flesh, the Bible then explains that this refers to Of the fowl after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind (v. 20). This includes all animals of the field and all large and small animals that are born via sexual intercourse. It excludes living things not born by coupling, and marine animals. Fish are excluded although they are considered “flesh.” Proof of this can be seen in the words of Moshe: and yet Thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month. If flocks and herds be slain for them…or if all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, will they suffice them (Bamidbar 11:21,22).
[Shalt thou bring into the ark.] This is a command to Noach not to desert these creatures but to bring them into the ark with him in order to preserve the seed of each species.

[Shall come unto thee.] They will come by themselves. Noach therefore did not have to search for them on islands; neither did he have to hunt for all sorts of fowl. Hashem commanded Noach to prepare food for all the animals in the ark. Foolish ones ask, what did birds of prey eat? What did carnivorous animals such as lions who live on meat eat? Their questions are invalid. One who cannot find meat will eat grass or fruit when hungry. The saying found in Rabbinic literature that there exists a large animal that consumes the grazing of one thousand mountains daily is a good story. Similarly the tradition concerning a bird that blocks out the sun with its wings has a secret meaning to it and is not to be taken literally. Hashem commanded Noach to make the ark many years before the flood. When the flood approached, Hashem the glorious commanded Noach and his family to go to the ark. Hashem the glorious commanded Noach to take seven males and seven females from every clean animal and fowl because they were needed for sacrifices.

For yet seven days. On the seventh day the rain will fall without letup for forty days. The Lord told this to Noach on the tenth day of the second month. At the end of the forty days from the start of the flood the sun returned to its proper place vis-a-vis the moon. The latter is a secret.

[Living substance.] The word yekum (living substance) is found in the Bible only in our chapter. It is a peh, yod and follows the paradigm of the word keruv (cherub). Others say that yekum is an inverted ayin, vav. It is like the word yerivai in Strive (riv) O Hashem, with them that strive with me (yerivai) (Tehillim 35:1). Living substance is a general term for every living thing that is upon the face of the earth.
And Noach did. As he was commanded. He and his family came to the vicinity of the ark.

Because of the waters of the flood. Because of fear of the waters of the flood. In these seven days many of the clean animals and fowl came of their own volition to the vicinity of the ark. From the others and from everything that creeps, a pair consisting of a male and female of each kind came to the ark.
Were all the fountains of the great deep broken up. Mayenot (fountains of) is in the construct. In When there were no fountains (mayanot) (Mishlei 8:24), mayanot is in the absolute.

Deep. The word tehom (deep) may be either masculine or feminine. Similarly tehom in The deep (tehom) made it grow (Yechezkel 31:4), is in the feminine. The Bible does not mention the streams because their waters come from the fountains. When the fountains of the deep broke up, their waters gushed upward and the windows of the heavenly storehouse of water were opened and their contents poured down upon the earth. The earth was confounded; there was no way of telling day from night. Proof of the latter is Hashem’s promise to Noach after the flood that and day and night shall not cease (Bereshit 8:22). When the rain ceased falling from the heavens, Noach knew that forty days and forty nights had passed, for Hashem revealed to him this secret.

And the windows of heaven. The word arubbot (windows) has the same meaning as arubbot (window) in Behold, if Hashem should make windows (arubbot) in heaven (Melachim II 7:2). The term window or storehouse (Devarim 28:12) when referring to heaven is in keeping with human language and practice. Some say that the alef of arubbot (windows) is a root letter and that arubbot is similar to kevudot (riches). Others say that the alef of arubbot is not a root letter. It is similar to the alef in agorat (piece of) (Shmuel I 2:36). Both arubbot and agorat come from roots whose last two letters are the same. On the seventeenth day of the second month, the day the flood started, Noach and his family entered the ark. At that time Noach brought into the ark the animals, cattle and the creeping things and fowl. Bird is a general term for a winged creature. The great miracle was that they all came two by two of their own volition.
And they that went in, went in male and female. The meaning of And they that went in is: and they that went into the ark.

[And Hashem shut him in.] The term shut him in in our verse has a positive connotation. It has to be so interpreted because being shut in at that time was preferable to not being shut in. However, elsewhere it has a negative implication. Thus we read, He shutteth up a man (Iyov 12:14), and And whom Hashem hath hedged in (Iyov 3:23). That it has a negative connotation is obvious from the first half of the verse. Noach closed the door of the ark and Hashem helped him in that no part of the ark cracked open, for had any part opened, then all would have immediately died. Why state, and the flood was forty days upon the earth (v. 17), after having said, And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights (v. 12)? The way to read the verse (v. 17) is as follows: After the flood was forty days upon the earth, the waters increased and bore up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth. This verse shows that for the first forty days the ark did not move.

Exceedingly. The word me’od (exceedingly) is repeated in the text in order to stress that the waters prevailed to their maximum potential. Why state, and the mountains were covered (v. 20), after having said, and all the high mountains that were under the whole heaven were covered (v. 19)? Its meaning is: All the high mountains were covered with water (v. 19), and these mountains were covered by fifteen cubits of water (v. 20). There are those who maintain that there is a very tall mountain in Yavan that the waters did not cover. However, we believe the words of our Elokim and we put aside the foolish nonsense of man.

[And all flesh perished.] The meaning of And all flesh perished is: and all flesh had perished. There are many such instances in Scripture, such as And I besought the Lord (Devarim 3:23), and the true meaning of And He caused manna to rain upon them for food (Tehillim 78:24).

[Perished.] Va-yigva (perished) means died. I will explain the exact meaning of this term when I comment on And Avraham expired (va-yigva), and died (Bereshit 25:8). It is clear that remes (creeping thing) is a general term that includes fowl, cattle, animals, small thin swarming things and man. It is possible that all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life (v. 22) refers to every man (v. 21), as we do not find the expression neshamah (breath) used in reference to any creature except man. Many say that the soul is termed neshamah because it comes from the heaven (shamayim). The fact that shamayim and neshamah have differing roots does not refute the latter interpretation because there are other similar instances.

And they were blotted out. Their names were erased from the earth because they left no descendants. [AND NOAH ONLY WAS LEFT.] Only Noach and those with him were left. This verse proves how wrong are some of our ignorant brethren who maintain that the flood did not cover the entire earth.

And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days. This was so because the fountains were broken up (v. 11) and it rained for a day and stopped for a day for, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights (v. 4) means it will rain for a period of forty days and forty nights without letup. That it did in fact also rain after the first forty days were over is evident from and the rain from heaven was restrained (Bereshit 8:2).
And Elokim remembered Noach. This includes his children and the women. Noach alone is mentioned because he was the most important of them.

And every living thing. A general term for beasts of the field, fowl that fly, and for everything that swarms upon the earth.And God remembered means God remembered the oath that he had sworn to Noach.
And Elokim made a wind to pass over the earth. The wind blew continuously.

And the waters assuaged. They rested and no longer prevailed. Then was the king’s wrath assuaged (Esther 7:10) is similar. Assuaged in our verse and in Esther is in the kal. However, in our verse the caf receives a dagesh to make up for the missing middle root letter.

Were stopped. Va-yissakheru (were stopped) is synonymous with va-yissageru (were closed). Although both of these words mean the same, they come from different roots. They do not come from one root with the caf and gimel interchanging, for these two letters do not interchange. The only letters that interchange are the yod, heh, vav and alef, and the sin and shin.
And the rain from heaven was restrained. It was restrained in the storehouse of rain.

And the waters returned. The waters returned at the end of one hundred and fifty days to their reservoirs beneath the earth where they are normally stored. Noach knew that it took one hundred and fifty days for this to happen, for he was a prophet. They err who maintain that since Scripture speaks of one hundred and fifty days making up five months, it must be referring to solar months, for five solar months come to one hundred and fifty-two days. Also anyone who maintains that Noach followed a calendar of intercalated lunar months, with Cheshvan being the second month and the year full, misses the mark. Why go to all this trouble? Even if the Bible explicitly stated that Noach employed solar months or that he counted the months from Tishrei this would have no effect on Jewish law, for the laws governing the establishment of the seasons were not given by Noach. It is also possible to say many things concerning the ark’s coming to rest. However, such speculations “cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain” (Shmuel I 12:21).

In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, were the tops of the mountains seen. Noach established the first day of the month even though he did not see the new moon, for he had not as yet opened the window of the ark. Noach sent out the raven on the tenth day of Shevat. From that day on the raven continuously went to and fro until Noach left the ark, for Scripture states that it went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth. On the day that the earth dried, Noach and all that were with him left the ark. Seven days after sending the raven, Noach sent the dove. The latter event took place on the seventeenth day of Shevat, which was the tenth month from the start of the flood. Noach observed the quarterly watch. And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove (v. 10) is proof of the above.

[And he stayed.] Va-yachel (and he stayed) is, I believe, derived from the word techillah (beginning). For if it came from the same root as tochelet (hope), it should have been vocalized va-yichel, as is the case with va-yiketz (and he awoke), or vocalized va-yechel, as in the case of va-yeshev (and he dwelt). However, it is possible it is an irregular verb.
And again he sent forth the dove out of the ark. On the twenty-fourth day of Shevat.

In her mouth an olive-leaf freshly plucked. Some say that Scripture employs two words with one meaning, as it does in the dust of the earth (Daniel 12:2). They interpret taraf (freshly plucked) as leaf. All its sprouting leaves (tarpe tzimchah) (Yechezkel 17:9) is similar. That taraf is a noun is evident from the long kamatz beneath the resh. It is like zahav (gold) and ashan (smoke). However, in my opinion the bet of be-fihah (mouth) is superfluous. It is like the bet of be-rucho (by his breath) in By His breath the heavens are serene (Iyov 26:13) and the bet of ve-echad (at one with Himself) (Iyov 23:13). In this case taraf is a verb meaning plucked and is vocalized with a kamatz beneath the second radical like taraf (torn) in For He hath torn (taraf) (Hoshea 6:1) and sha’ag (hath roared) in The lion hath roared (sha’ag) (Amos 3:8) and other similar cases. It is also possible that taraf (freshly plucked) is vocalized with a kamatz because it is an adjective like chacham (wise). It means the same as taruf (torn), for an adjective may resemble an active or passive participle.

And he stayed. Va-yiyyachel (and he stayed) is a nifal and is penultimately accented like va-yillachem (and he fought) (Bamidbar 21:1) and va-yitzamed (and he was joined) (Bamidbar 25:3). However, there are instances when corresponding nifals are accented on the last syllable, as in va-yippaked (was empty) in that David’s place was empty (Shmuel I 20:27). The entire root appears in And he stayed, as it does in shot through (yiyyareh) (Shemot 19:13).
[And sent forth the dove.] Noach sent out the dove on the first day of Adar. This time it no longer returned to him as it was wont to.
Any more. Od (anymore) means forever. Od in his uncleanness is yet (od) upon him (Bamidbar 19:13) and While the earth remaineth (od kol yeme ha-aretz) (Bereshit 8:22) is similar.

The waters were dried up from off the earth. Only the surface of the earth dried; the soil itself was swampy and hence not yet firm enough to walk upon. The earth did not fully dry until later. Those who insist that Noach used a lunar calendar because Scripture tells us that he spent a year and ten days in the ark and the ten days refer to the excess of the solar year over a lunar year are pressing a point. First of all, for this to be so the year had to be “full.” Furthermore, there is no reason to assume that Noach spent a year in the ark. He could equally have been in it for a solar year plus ten days.

Bring forth. Haytze (bring forth) is written as if it came from a root whose radicals remain unchanged in conjugation. Hayshar (make straight) in Make Thy way straight before my face (Tehillim 5:9) is similar.
That they may swarm. Reproduce.

After their families. After their kind. Some say that the animals bred in the ark. Each family then left the ark by itself and did not intermingle with any other. This interpretation is not farfetched.

Every clean beast. There are ten kinds of clean beasts. We do not know the number of clean fowl because the Bible lists only the unclean ones since the clean fowl are more numerous than the unclean. Noach built the altar on one of the mountains of Ararat.

Smelled. Va-yarach (smelled) follows the paradigm of va-yanach (rested) in and rested (va-yanach) in all the borders of Mitzrayim (Shemot 10:14). The resh is vocalized with a pattach because the chet which follows it is a guttural. This is in keeping with the rules of Hebrew grammar. Heaven forbid that one conclude from our verse that Hashem smells. Neither does He eat, as Who did eat the fat of their sacrifices (Devarim 32:38) states. The meaning of our verse is that Hashem accepted the burnt offering and it pleased Him. It may be compared to a human being who smells a pleasant scent and enjoys it.

The sweet savour. Nicho’ach (sweet savour) comes from the same root as menuchah (rest). The chet is doubled in nicho’ach as the final peh of the root of ve-na’afufe’ah (and her adulteries) is doubled (Hoshea 2:4). Its meaning is that the sweet odor assuaged God’s anger, or that it caused a power from on high to rest on man.
In his heart. El libbo means in His heart. He then revealed His secret to Noach who was a prophet.
[I will not again curse the ground.] As I did on account of Adam, as it is written, cursed is the ground for thy sake (Bereshit 3:17).
The imagination. Yetzer (the imagination) refers to the nature that man was created with.
Neither will I again smite. Via a flood.
[Again.] Od means forever, or again. And wept on his neck a good while (od) (Bereshit 46:29) is similar.

While the earth remaineth. This indicates that an end has been fixed for the earth. The Rabbinic interpretation of It shall be eighteen thousand reeds round about (Yechezkel 48:38) is very precious. However, even one in a thousand does not know what it means.

Seed time and harvest. The year is divided into two periods and then into four: cold, the antithesis of heat, and summer, the antithesis of winter, corresponding to the four seasons of the year. The four periods are all divided into day and night, for when the days are short the nights are long, and as the nights get shorter the days get longer until both are equal.

And the dread of you. The root of ve-chittechem (and the dread of you) is chet, tav, tav. It comes from the same root as chatat (terror) in Ye, see a terror (chatat) (Iyov 6:21). Chittechem is synonymous with chatattekhem.
And upon all wherewith the ground teemeth. It means everything which creeps upon the ground. Or, ha’adamah (the ground) is the subject.
Into your hand are they delivered. This is to be read as if written, “because” into your hand are they delivered.
[And upon all.] Some say that the bet of be-khol (and upon all) and of u-ve-khol (and upon all) are in place of a vav. However, it is more likely that this clause is connected to And the fear of you.
Every moving thing. Remes (moving thing) is a general term for wild and domesticated animals and for all fowl and fish. Man was now permitted to kill and eat them all.

As the green herb. Yerek (green) can be vocalized in two ways. The same is true with smoke. We thus find, behold a smoking (ashan) furnace (Bereshit 15:17), and as the smoke (ke-eshen) of a furnace (Ex. 19:18).

Only flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat. The meaning of this verse is that you shall not eat flesh with its life (nefesh), which is its blood, as in and thou shalt not eat the life (nefesh, i.e., the blood) with the flesh (Devarim 12:23), and For as to the life (nefesh) of all flesh, the blood thereof is all one with the life (nefesh) thereof (Vayikra 17:14). The nefesh (life) which moves and feels is the body.

And surely your blood of your lives will I require. I have permitted you to shed the blood of all living creatures. However, I have prohibited you the spilling of the blood of your lives because you are human. On the contrary, I will avenge that blood (edreshennu), as in For He that avengeth (doresh) blood (Tehillim 9:13). Scripture first lays down a general rule, And surely your blood of your lives will I require, and then goes into detail and tells us whom God will punish for taking human life. AND AT THE HAND OF MAN. If many people kill one person or if one man kills another person (even at the hand of every man’s brother), I will avenge that death. I will also punish a beast that kills a man by having another animal kill it. Thus man is permitted to kill animals but animals are prohibited from killing humans. In my opinion it is farfetched to maintain that and surely your blood of your lives refers to suicide.

[Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed.] This is a further elaboration. It may also be taken, and this appears most likely, as a command to the sons of Noach to execute murderers. The term ba-adam (by man) can be interpreted in one of three ways: in front of witnesses; in front of people; or because a man was killed. There are many other such instances.
And Elokim spoke unto Noach, and to his sons. Elokim spoke to Noach’s sons through Noach. It is also possible that they were all prophets and Elokim addressed all four of them.

And with your seed. Ve-et zarakhem is to be rendered: and with your seed. The third with you (v. 10) is to be interpreted as meaning: that were with you. It is also possible that with you is repeated for additional explanation. The covenant spoken of is that all flesh not be cut off anymore by the waters of the flood (v. 11).

[Neither shall all flesh be cut off.] Flesh refers to the body. The body is so designated because flesh senses and the bones do not. The covenant is a promise that all bodies will never again be destroyed by a flood. God included in His covenant a pledge not to bring a comparable deluge ever again because the first part of His promise, neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of the flood, may be taken to imply that there will be other floods but that God will save humanity. It is concerning this covenant that the prophet says, For as I have sworn that the waters of Noach Should no more go over the earth (Is. 54:9).
The token. Ot (token) may be either masculine or feminine.
My bow. Behold, I now set a bow in the clouds. Saadiah Gaon’s interpretation that the rainbow was previously in existence is incorrect.

When I bring clouds over the earth. The nun of be-aneni (when I bring clouds) does not have a dagesh even though it is a pi’el and therefore should have a dagesh in the middle radical of the root, as in when I speak (be-dabberi) with thee (Shemot 19:9).

And the bow is seen in the clouds. If we would believe what the Greek scholars tell us, that the rainbow is produced by the sun’s flames, then we must assume that after the flood Hashem strengthened the sun’s light. This is the way that a person who understands the sciences will interpret this verse.

[And the waters shall no more become.] The use of the singular yiheyeh (shall become) with mayim (waters) does not prove that mayim is singular. We find the same word used with a plural in But there were (va-yehi) certain men (Bamidbar 9:6).
[And the bow shall be in the cloud.] The bow is always hidden in the cloud and there seen by Hashem.
And Elokim said unto Noach. This is the covenant that I disclosed to you and this is the oath which I have established.

And Cham is the father of Kenaan. This teaches that both Cham and Kenaan were wicked, and as the father does, so do the children. Kenaan and not Kush is mentioned in this verse because Kenaan was going to be cursed. This chapter was written to inform us that all Kenaani, both male and female, bear a curse from the time of Noach. Avraham thus commanded his servant, thou shalt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Kenaani (Bereshit 24:3). Rivkah similarly said, If Yaakov takes a wife of the daughters of Chet…what good shall my life do me (Bereshit 27:46). Should someone ask, what sins were the Chiti guilty of, let him open his eyes; the Chiti and the Emori and the others are all descendants of Kenaan. We therefore read, unto the land of Kenaan (Yehoshua 22:32).

And Noach…began. Va-yachel (began) is derived from techillah (beginning). It belongs to those roots whose second and third letters are identical. It is a hifil, similar to va-yasekh (shut up) in Or who shut up (va-yasekh) the sea with doors (Iyov 38:8).

The husbandman. A skilled agriculturalist, agriculture being a great science. The Rabbinic statement that Noach drank from his vineyard on the day he planted it is not to be taken literally. There is a secret meaning to it. Similarly and the woman conceived, and bore a son (Shemot 2:2) did not take place on one and the same day.

And he was uncovered. Va-yitgal (and he was uncovered) comes from the root gimel, lamed, heh, meaning to uncover. It is a hitpa’el. Yital (lift himself up) in And let him lift himself up (yital) (Yirmiyahu 51:3) is similar.

[His tent.] The heh of oholoh (his tent) is in place of a vav. The heh of be-re’oh (as they shouted), in the noise of the people as they shouted (be-re’oh) (Shemot 32:17), and the heh of fera’oh (let them loose) in for Aharon had let them loose (fera’oh) (Shemot 32:25), are similar.
Upon both their shoulders. Each one placed an edge of the blanket on his shoulders. Shekhem (shoulders) does not come in the plural.
Backward. Opposite of the normal way of walking, which is to go forward.

And Noach awoke. Scripture does not reveal what was done to Noach. Be that as it may, Kenaan was the culprit. The sequence of events was as follows: Cham saw his father’s nakedness and unlike his brothers did not cover him. On the contrary, he revealed what he saw. Kenaan heard that Noach was lying naked in his tent and did something to Noach. However, the Bible does not tell us what he did to him.

The meaning of the verse and (Noach) knew what his youngest son had done unto him is proof that Kenaan was the culprit, for we read, And the sons of Cham: Kush, and Mitzrayim, and Put, and Kenaan (Bereshit 10:6). Furthermore, the his in his youngest son refers to Cham, who is previously mentioned. That is why Noach cursed Kenaan. The one who says that Cham was the culprit, and that Kenaan was cursed because Noach did not want to curse his son (Cham) because Elokim had blessed Noach’s sons, is indulging in Midrash.

A servant of servants. Eved avadim (a servant of servants) means a servant like all other servants. If Scripture meant a servant to servants then it would have read eved ha-avadim. Proof of this is: it is most holy (kodesh kodashim) (Vayikra 6:18), and In a most holy place (be-kodesh ha-kodashim) (Bamidbar 18:10).

[Unto his brethren.] To Kush, Mitzrayim and Put, the sons of Cham his father. There are some who say that the Kushim are enslaved because Noach cursed Cham. However, they have forgotten that the first king to rule after the flood was a Kushi. Thus it is written, and Kush begot Nimrod…And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Arkovaye, and Akad, and Kalne, in the land of Shinar (Bereshit 10:8-10).

Blessed be Hashem, the Elokim of Shem. We are duty-bound to be bountiful in praise of Hashem, who is the Elokim of Shem, for He will make Kenaan a servant of Elokim and Shem. The meaning of our verse is, Elokim will compel Kenaan to serve Shem, for lamo (their) has the same meaning as la-hem (to them). The vav of lamo is superfluous and is similar to the vav of tevi’emo (Thou bringest them in) (Shemot 15:17). Therefore the term “to them” is not encountered in Scripture, spelled either without a heh or a vav. The Tetragrammaton is invoked in connection with Shem to honor Shem. It is not employed with regard to Yefet because he was not his brother’s equal. Saadiah Gaon says that Cursed be Kenaan is short for cursed be Kenaan’s father. He says that In the presence of Chanamel my uncle (Yirmiyahu 32:12) is similar, as Chanamel was really Yirmiyahu’s uncle’s son. However, it is possible that Chanamel was older than Yirmiyahu and the latter referred to him as “my uncle” because it was an honor for him to be called by his father’s title. Similarly one’s father’s brother’s wife is called aunt in Scripture. However, in our case there is no reason to refer to Cham by the name of his son.

[Enlarge.] Saadiah also explains the word yaft (enlarge) as coming from the Hebrew word for beautiful (yafeh). However, his comment is not beautiful (yafeh). Yaft means he will enlarge. The Aramaic word for He shall enlarge (Devarim 12:20) is similar. Yaft (enlarge) is a hifil. It is like yard in And maketh him rule (yard) over kings (Is. 41:2). Both Shem and Yefet were blessed in this verse, for the meaning of And he shall dwell in the tents of Shem is: may Elokim dwell in the tents of Shem. The previous verse (v. 26) relates the blessing with which Noach blessed Hashem.

And let Kenaan be their servant. To Shem, to Yefet and also to his brothers. Thus Kenaan was to be a slave to all of the world, for from Shem, Yefet and Kenaan’s brothers all of humanity is descended. This came to pass many years after the flood.
Kitim. Kitim is the name of one of Yavan’s sons. I therefore explain in my comments on the Book of Daniel that Greeks and Romans constitute one kingdom.
Nimrod. Do not attempt to ascertain the meaning of any names encountered in the Bible if Scripture itself does not explain them.
Nimrod was the first to display man’s power over the wild beasts for he was a mighty hunter.

The meaning of before Hashem (v. 9) is that Nimrod built altars and offered the animals he hunted as whole offerings to Hashem. This is the literal meaning of the verse. However, its Midrashic interpretation is totally different.
Wherefore it is said. This proverb was also used in the days of Moshe.

[Out of that land went forth Ashur.] Ashur was the son of Yefet. The events related in this verse took place after the dispersion following the building of the Tower of Babel. Nimrod was the first king over Babel. According to Seder Olam, Nimrod was king over the seventy who built the tower, and it was in his time that the dispersion took place.
The same is the great city. It appears to me that this is connected to and builded Nineveh. However, it is also possible that it is connected to Resen or Kalach.

And mizraim begot Ludim. In my opinion, these are the names of countries, each of which was populated by a particular family. This is why all the names (in verses 13 and 14) are in the plural. Proof of this is the name Patrusim. Additional and definite proof that this interpretation is correct is the phrase whence went forth (v. 14), for the word whence alludes to a place.

[And caphtorim.] Mitzrayim also begat the Kaftorim. The term begat is used in Scripture when referring to the father because the child comes from the strength and power of the father and is in his likeness and image.
As thou goest toward Gerar. The word gerarah means to Gerar.
These are the sons of Cham, after their families, after their tongues. Scripture says the same concerning the children of Yefet and the children of Shem.

[The father of all the children of Ever.] Scripture informs us that Shem was the father of the Hebrews for no one was greater than he, and Hashem was his Elokim. Similarly it is written, Thus saith Hashem, the Elokim of the Hebrews (ivrim) (Shemot 10:3). On the other hand, the Bible tells us that Cham was the father of Kenaan for no one was baser that he. It is unfitting for the holy and profane to intermingle.

Scripture notes that Shem was the brother of Yefet the elder to teach us that Yefet, too, was a worthy person. The Bible lists Shem, who was the youngest, before Yefet, who was the elder, out of respect to Shem. Proof that Yefet was the elder lies in Scripture’s stating that Noach was five hundred years old when he begat his first son. There is no room for argument, for it is clear that Noach had no children prior to reaching the age of five hundred. The flood came when Noach was six hundred years old. Therefore if Shem was the eldest he would be one hundred and one years old when Noach and his sons came out of the ark. However, Scripture tells us Shem was a hundred years old, and begot Arpachshad two years after the flood (Bereshit 11:10). Others say that Shem was the elder brother of Yefet, and it is for this reason that Shem is mentioned first. They explain that Shem was born a few days after Noach entered his five hundredth year, for even a day in a year is considered a year. They say that Noach was born in Iyyar and Shem in Sivan. When the flood came Noach was five hundred and ninety-nine plus a number of days old. Hence Shem was not a full ninety-nine years old when the flood started and was a hundred and one years plus a number of months old when his son Arpachshad was born. The meaning of two years after the flood (Bereshit 11:10) therefore is to be interpreted as meaning that Arpachshad was born in the second year following the beginning of the flood. There are also those who maintain that the wife of Shem conceived five months after the start of the flood when the waters started decreasing. Shem was thus one hundred years old when Arpachshad was born. There are ten similar instances in the Book of Melachim.

One language. When the word one in the feminine is in the absolute it is vocalized with a segol beneath the alef (echat). However, when it is in the construct it is vocalized with a pattach beneath the alef (achat). In my book on grammar I have explained why the dalet is missing in the feminine word for one. A logical reading of Scripture indicates that the dispersion took place one hundred years after the flood, and that Peleg, which means divided, was so named because at the time of his birth the earth was divided (Bereshit 10:25). Peleg is similar to palga, the Aramaic word for half. Palge (rivers) in rivers of water (palge mayim) (Tehillim 119:136) is identical. It refers to the branches into which the river divides. The names given to Ichavod (Shmuel I 4:21) and Immanuel, who was the son of the prophet Yeshayahu (Is. 7:14), are similar. Nevertheless, the words of the Seder Olam are also correct, and we will rely upon them. If this is so, then Avraham was one of the builders of the tower of Babel. Do not be amazed at this, for Noach and Shem were also there. Indeed, Shem didn’t die till Yaakov was over fifty. The meaning of safah echat is one language. It appears to me that the one language was Hebrew. Proof of this are the names Adam, Chavah, Kayin, Shet and Peleg.

[And of one speech.] Unlike today, when there are words which not everybody speaking a given language will understand, the learned and the ignorant in those days spoke alike.Achadim (one) is the plural of echad.
[As they journeyed east.] This verse shows that the mountains of Ararat are in the east.

[That they found a plain.] Its meaning is, they searched for a good place to build a state. Eventually they found this plain. The meaning of bikah (plain) is a flat area; it is the opposite of the rough places (Is. 40:4). As the cattle go down into the valley (Ba-bikah) (Is. 63:14) is similar. Bikah possibly refers to a plain between mountains because a valley appears to be a split in the hills.

Let us make brick. Nilbenah (let us make brick) comes from the same root as levenim (bricks). Even though levenim ends in a mem, it is a feminine word. Such irregular feminine plural endings are also found in the words nashim (women) and pilagshim (concubines). They baked the bricks until they became hard. A building made from such material is very strong and will not dissolve in water or fall apart when burned.
And they had brick for stone. In place of stone.

And slime. In place of mortar. The meaning of chemar (slime) is the same as its Arabic cognate. The builders of the tower were not fools to believe that they could actually ascend the heavens. Neither were they afraid that Hashem would bring another flood, for Noach and his children, to whom the Almighty swore never to bring another deluge, were there and being descendents of Noach and his children they were subservient to them. Scripture reveals their intention and ultimate goal. They wanted to build a great city to dwell in, and a very tall tower to ensure their fame and glory and to serve as a sign indicating the place of the city to those outside it, such as shepherds. The tower, as long as it stood, would also perpetuate their names after their deaths. This is the meaning of and let us make us a name.

The word havah (come) means give; its root is yod, heh, bet, as is clear from Cast thy burden (yehavecha) upon Hashem (Tehillim 55:23). Because haveh is used often, it remains the same in both the feminine and the plural. Compare, come (havah), let us deal wisely with them (Shemot 1:10), and Come (havah), I pray thee, let me come in unto thee (Bereshit 38:16).

Do not be surprised at the phrase with its top in heaven. Moshe similarly said, the cities are great and fortified up to heaven (Devarim 1:28). The builders of the tower hoped that their city and tower would prevent them from dispersing, but this was not Hashem’s will. However, they did not know this.

[And Hashem came down.] The Bible states this because all things on earth below are dependent upon the powers on high; all actions are arranged from heaven. Therefore Hashem is referred to as the One Who rideth upon the heaven (Devarim 33:26) and the One who is enthroned in the heavens (Tehillim 123:1). The use of the term And Hashem came down is an anthropomorphism.

And Hashem said: behold, they are one people. Hashem said this to the angels. This took place before And Hashem came down. Its meaning is: And Hashem came down because he said, Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language, etc.

One people. They have one religion. Different religions create jealousy and hatred among people. The same is true with regard to different languages. That is why the king of Paras and Madai commanded that every man should bear rule in his own house, and speak according to the language of his people (Es. 1:22). The heh of hachillam (what they begin) is vocalized with a pattach because of the chet which follows it.
The heh should have been vocalized with a chataf pattach as is the rule concerning all double roots in the hifil perfect. The heh of hachiloti (I have begun) (Devarim 2:31) is similarly vocalized.

[Withholden.] Yibbatzer means will be withholden. Betzurot (fortified) in fortified (betzurot) cities (Devarim 3:5) is like it. The meaning of our verse is: If I permit them to go on, they will think that they can do whatever they wish.
[They purpose.] Yazemu (they purpose) has the same meaning as zamemu (devised). However, they come from different roots.
Come, let us go down. This is what Hashem said to the angels.

[And there confound their language.] All the grammarians claim that ve-navelah (and confound) is a nifal. They compare it to ve-navekah (and shall be made empty) in And the spirit of Mitzrayim shall be made empty (ve-navekah) (Is. 19:3) and to navelah (fadeth) in The earth fainteth and fadeth away (navelah) (Is. 24:4). However, their interpretation is farfetched. Why would the Bible say: Come, let us go down and their language will be confounded, when their language was not confounded because Hashem and the angels went down? Ve-navelah can only be interpreted as an active verb. Proof of this is Scripture’s stating at the close of this incident, because Hashem did there confound the language of all the earth (v. 9). The following is then the grammatical explanation of ve-navelah. It is a hifil. Scripture should have employed the entire root and read ve-navlilah, or ve-navellah if one of the two lameds of its double root was swallowed. In the latter case it would have followed the paradigm of ve-nasebbah (let us bring back) in and let us bring back (ve-nasebbah) the ark of our Hashem (Divrei Hayamim I 13:3). Our word reads ve-navelah because one of the lameds of the root was dropped without the remaining lamed receiving a dagesh forte to make up for it. The sages who translated the Torah into Greek correctly rendered ve-navelah as I will confound, rather than we will confound. If the above mentioned grammarians are correct, why did the sages omit the nun? Some say that the people building the tower started hating each other and each one invented a new language. Others say that the One who grants knowledge to man caused them to forget their language. In my opinion, they were first scattered. After their dispersion Nimrod ruled over Babel and other kings arose. With the passage of time and the death of the first generation to be scattered, the original language was forgotten. Hashem scattered the people for their own benefit. He similarly said, and replenish the earth (Bereshit 1:28).

[And they left off to build the city.] Its meaning is: they left off from completing the city because part of the city and the tower had by this time been built. This is so for Scripture reads, the city and the tower, which the children of men builded (v. 5). It is also possible that the meaning of which the children of men builded is: which the children of men intended to build. Then Balak the son of Tzipor, king of Moav, arose and fought against Yisrael (Yehoshua 24:9) is similar. The first of these interpretations appeals to me.
Babel. Bavel (Babel) is made up of the words ba (came) and bel (confusion), with the alef missing. Bagad (Fortune is come) (Bereshit 30:11) and Bamah (high place) (Yechezkel 20:29) are similar.

[Two years after the flood.] I have already explained the meaning of this in the verse the elder brother of Yefet (Bereshit 10:21). It is possible that Peleg was given this name on the day of his death, the reason for this being as follows: Shem lived for five hundred years following the flood, Arpachshad lived for four hundred and thirty-eight years, his son Shelah lived four hundred and thirty-three years, and his son Ever four hundred and sixty-four years. Now Peleg lived two hundred and thirty-nine years. Thus Peleg’s life span was half that of his ancestors. Reu, the son of Peleg, similarly lived to the same age as Peleg. Reu’s son Srug also lived about the same number of years as Peleg and Reu. This, then, is the general rule: no one after Peleg, aside from his son, ever lived to be two hundred and thirty-nine years. Some say that those who built the tower numbered seventy and hence were divided into seventy languages upon their dispersion. If you count the sons of Shem, Yefet and Cham you will find them to be seventy. However, they are incorrect. First of all Patrusim and Kasluchim are not the names of two individuals. Furthermore, they neglect to include in the seventy Noach and his sons. According to the Seder Olam the builders of the tower numbered thousands and ten thousands.

[And begot Avram.] Avraham was born in a place called Ur of the Chaldees. Therefore glorify ye Hashem in the regions of light (be-urim) (Is. 24:15) is like it. It appears to me that at the time of Avraham’s birth Ur of the Chaldees had another name since the Chaldees are descended from Nachor, the brother of Avraham, and that in writing the Torah Moshe used the name in vogue in his time when he cited Ur of the Chaldees. Proof that Avraham was born in Ur of the Chaldees can be found in the fact that Haran died there and Scripture says, And Haran died…in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees (v. 20). It is also possible that the Chaldees made a flame (altar) and the place thereof was called Ur (the flame, altar) of the Chaldees. In this instance Ur has the meaning of fire, as in whose fire (ur) is in Tziyon (Is. 31:9).
[In the presence of.] In front of his father; i.e., Terach witnessed his death. In the presence of Aharon their father (Bamidbar 3:4) is analogous.

[And the name of nahor’s wife, milcah.] The Bible gives the name of Nachor’s wife in order to let us know the pedigree of Rivkah, Rachel and Leah. Our sages, of blessed memory, identified Yiskah with Sarah. If this is a tradition we will accept it. Those who say that Avraham rather than Sarah was sterile are saying the opposite of what Scripture says. Additional proof that they are wrong is the fact that Avraham sired Yishmael and had children with Keturah.I do not find the explanation of those who say that Sarah was Avraham’s sister to be acceptable. If Sarah was really Avraham’s sister, Scripture would have stated, And Terach took Avram his son, and Sarai his daughter, the wife of Avram his son. Similarly if Sarah was the sister of Lot the Bible would have stated, “and Sarai the daughter of his son,” as it does in the case of Lot. It is possible that Terach’s son Nachor left for Charan before his father. On the other hand he may have left for Charan after his father went there. It appears to me that the portion containing the command, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto the land that I will show thee (Bereshit 12:1), was conveyed to Avraham before what is recorded in the verse reading, And Terach took Avram…Lot…Sarai…to go into the land of Kenaan. Similarly elsewhere the Pentateuch states, And Hashem spoke unto Moshe in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they were come out of the land of Mitzrayim (Bamidbar 1:1); and then, And it came to pass in the first month in the second year (Shemot 40:17). Proof of the above is found in And they went forth…to go into the land of Kenaan (v. 31). When Terach came to Charan, the place found favor in his eyes. He settled there and eventually died there. The general rule thus is that the Bible does not always list events in chronological order.

Get thee out. Hashem commanded Avraham while he was yet in Ur of the Chaldees to leave his country, his place of birth and also his father’s house. The reason Hashem told Avraham to leave his father’s house is that Hashem knew that, although he set out for Kenaan, Terach would settle in Charan. Terach did not die until sixty years after Avraham left his father’s house in Charan. However, the Bible does not tell us how old he was when he left Ur of the Chaldees. After telling Avraham to go unto the land that I will show thee, Hashem revealed his secret to him, for we read: and they went forth to go into the land of Kenaan (v. 5). It is also possible that I will show thee refers to for all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it (Bereshit 13:15).
Them that bless thee. This word is in the plural.
And him that curseth thee. This word is in the singular.
Their substance. Their cattle. Rekhusham (their substance) in And the land was not able to bear them…for their (rekhusham) substance (i.e., their cattle) was great (Bereshit 13:6) is similar.

And the souls that they had gotten in Charan. Servants born into their household. It is also possible that had gotten means bought. Hath gotten in My power and the might of my hand hath gotten me this wealth (Devarim 8:17) is similar. Others say that the souls that they had gotten in Charan refers to the people to whom Avraham showed the truth, to worship Hashem.
[And they went forth to go.] To the place that Hashem had told them to go.
[Shechem.] Shechem was the name used by Moshe because it was the name by which the city was known in his time. Shechem was not yet born in Avraham’s day.
Terebinth. Eilon (terebinth) has the same meaning as elah (terebinth). They are trees. Others say that elon means a field, as in unto El paran (Bereshit 14:6).
Moreh. Some identify him with Mamre, the confederate of Avraham. However, it is possible they are not to be so identified and Eilon Moreh is the name of a place.

And the Kenaani was then in the land. It is possible that the Kenaani seized the land of Kenaan from some other tribe at that time. Should this interpretation be incorrect, then there is a secret meaning to the text. Let the one who understands it remain silent.

And Hashem appeared. In a prophetic vision. Va-yera (appeared) is a nifal. It is vocalized with a tzere to make up for the dagesh which should have been placed in the resh as compensation for the missing nun of the nifal conjugation.
Who appeared unto him. Nireh is a participle belonging to the above-mentioned conjugation (nifal). Na’aseh (prepared) in Now that which was prepared (na’aseh) for one day (Nechemyah 5:18) is similar.

And he removed. Va-yatek (and he removed) is a transitive verb, in the hifil. However, ve-yetak (removed) in Or shall the rock be removed (ve-yetak) out of its place (Iyov 18:4) is intransitive. The object of And he removed is his tent. His tent is also the object of he pitched. The meaning (of va-yatek) is: he caused to move. Va-yet (he pitched) is vocalized with a tzere to make up for the missing nun which is the first root letter of va-yet (he pitched). Ve-yez (is dashed) in And their lifeblood is dashed (ve-yez) (Is. 63:3) is similar. Both are transitive verbs.

[On the west.] The word mi-yam means on the west. Yam (sea) means west because the great Spanish Sea (yam, i.e., the Mediterranean) is the western border of the land of Yisrael. The latter sea is not the Atlantic, the Atlantic being far from the aforementioned country. Avraham journeyed from east of Beit El westward until Ai was east of his camp.
[And called upon the name of Hashem.] This means he prayed there. It may also mean that he called upon men to worship Hashem.

Toward the south. Negev means south and it means the same in Aramaic. Negev in Aramaic means dry as we see from Onkelos, who renders the waters were dried up (Bereshit 8:13) as negivu mayya. The south is called Negev (dry) because it is hot there, and the heat parches the land. This is the way for that thou hast set me in the Southlands (eretz ha-negev) give me therefore springs of water (Yehoshua 15:19) should be understood.
And there was a famine in the land. In the land of Kenaan.

When he was come near. When he caused his camp to come near. On the other hand, hikriv (when he came near) may be intransitive. These two interpretations are possible because there are verbs which can be transitive and intransitive.
[Now.] Na means now. Na in Behold now (na), I am old (Bereshit 27:2), and Woe (na) unto us (Eichah 5:16) are similar. The reverse of Hebrew is the case in Arabic.

[Behold now, I know.] There were women as beautiful as Sarah in her native country, but in Mitzrayim and the southern land there was none as beautiful. The reason for this is that people’s appearance is shaped by the climate.
[But thee they will keep alive.] They will provide for all of your needs. Avraham said this because those were days of famine.

[Thou art my sister.] Achoti (my sister) is penultimately accented because the word which follows it, at (thou), is accented on the first letter. Kara laylah (he called night) (Bereshit 1:5) is similar. The preceding is a general rule in Hebrew grammar. The tav of at (thou) receives a dagesh to make up for the missing nun, for the word at (thou) comes from the same root as ani (I).
Because of thee. Bi-glalekh (because of thee) and ba-avurekh (for thy sake) always have a bet prefixed to each. The poet who omits this bet errs.

[That it may be well with me.] They will give me gifts and presents. And so it is written, And he dealt well with Avram for her sake; and he had sheep, and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and maid-servant, and she-asses, and camels (v. 16).

[And praised]. The dagesh which should have been placed in the first lamed of va-yehalelu (and praised) is omitted in order to simplify the word’s pronunciation. Va-etpalelah (and I prayed) (Daniel 9:4) is identical.

And the woman was taken. Va-tukkach (and she was taken) is a hofal. This is so even though it is not found in the hifil. Va-tushlekhi (but thou wast cast out) (Yechezkel 16:5) is an example of a hofal wherein the entire root is present.
And Hashem plagued Paroh…because of Sarai. The term al devar means because. Al devar’s meaning is al zeh ha-davar (on account of this thing).
[Thou tell me.] The root of higgadta (thou tell) is nun, gimel, dalet.

[So I took her to be my wife.] This indicates that Paroh took her to be his wife, to sleep with her. Hashem brought plagues upon him to prevent him from touching her. Hashem sent these plagues to protect the wife of the one whom he loved. The plagues were so severe that Paroh was unable to touch Sarah. The following is analogous: When thou goest forth to battle against thine enemies…and seest among the captives a woman of goodly form, and thou hast a desire unto her, and takest her to thee to wife. The Bible then says, then thou shalt bring her home to thy house; and she shall shave her head. It then concludes, and after that thou mayest go in unto her (Devarim 21:10-13).

[And go thy way.] The vav of va-lekh (and go thy way) is vocalized with a kamatz because it is prefixed to a word with a cantillical note that ends a phrase. The vav of va-yayin (and wine) in bread and wine (Bereshit 14:18) is similar.
And they brought him on the way. They honorably escorted him. And Avraham went with them to bring them on the way (Bereshit 18:16) is similar.

[And Paroh gave men charge concerning him.] It appears to me that this clause indicates that Paroh issued a command to his people concerning Avraham. He warned and charged that it be announced that no one harm Avraham and his wife.
[And Avram went up.] I have grammatically explained the word va-ya’al (and went up) in my Book of Foundation.

And Avram was very rich. Ve-avram kaved me’od (literally, Avram was very heavy) means that Avraham had great wealth. Whoever is laden with riches moves heavily (with difficulty). Don’t you see that the Hebrew word for honor (kavod) comes from the same root as the word for heavy (koved) in A stone is heavy (koved even) (Mishlei 27:3). Conversely, the word for shame (kalon) comes from the same root as the word for light (kal). Compare, light of foot (kal beraglav) (Shmuel II 2:18). Avraham possessed herds of cattle and a large amount of gold and silver.
On his journeys. Avraham made many stops on his journey from the south to Beit El which is in the north. He came unto the place of the altar (v. 4) to give thanks to God for ensuring his safe return.

And tents. I believe that ohel (tent), in the singular, follows the paradigm of kodesh (holy). It is always found in Scripture following this form. In the plural, its alef is vocalized with a chataf kamatz, as in the verse ye shall dwell in tents (Yirmiyahu 35:7). It is vocalized like the word kodashim in he shall not eat of the holy things (ba-kodashim) (Vayikra 22:4). However, when the alef of the Hebrew plural for tents is vocalized with a cholam, the singular is vocalized like goral (lot). The latter is so even though this form for tent (ohal) is not found in Scripture.

Together. Yachdav (together) can refer to two (as in our verse) or to many, as in And all the people answered together (yachdav) (Shemot 19:8). This word does not follow the rules of Hebrew grammar. Yachdav is not synonymous with yachad (together). Yachdav means acting like one person.

[And the Kenaani and the perizzite dwelt then in the land.] This is to be understood as its counterpart (Bereshit 12:6). It is possible that Perizzi was a son of Kenaan and was included in the list of Kenaan’s sons under a different name. He, like the prophet Shmuel’s son and grandfather, had two names.
Then I will go to the right. Ve-e’minah (I will go to the right) comes from the same root as yamin (right).

[Then I will go to the left.] The alef of the noun semol (left) is enunciated in the verb ve-asme’ilah (then I will go to the left). Now this alef is missing in the word hasmili (direct thyself to the left) in Go thee one way to the right, or direct thyself to the left (Yechezkel 21:21). Thus, we cannnot determine whether the alef is part of the root of semol or not.

The plain of the Yarden. Kikkar (plain) means an area with plants. The caf is doubled in kikkar. On the other hand, it is possible that one caf has been dropped in kar nirchav (large pastures) (Is. 30:23). Similarly bat (apple of) in bat ayin (the apple of the eye) (Tehillim 17:8) is short for bavat in bavat eno (the apple of his eye) (Zecharyah 2:12).
Well watered. Mashkeh (watered) is masculine; khullah (well) is feminine. A fire not blown by man shall consume him (Iyov 20:26) is similar.
Before Hashem destroyed Sedom and Amorah. Shachet (destroyed) is an infinitive in the pi’el. The meaning of li-fene shachet is: before Hashem destroyed.
And lot journeyed. From the east, for Sedom is west of Beit El.
And moved his tent. Pitched his tent.
Now the men of Sedom were wicked. To their fellow man. This is stated in Yechezkel, viz., neither did she (Sedom) strengthen the hand of the poor and needy (Yechezkel 16:49).
For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it. By word. And he shall put them (Yisrael’s sins and transgressions) upon the head of the goat (Vayikra 16:21) is similar.
In this chapter Scripture informs us that the terebinths of Mamre are located in Chevron.

King of goiim. Goyim like Eilam is the name of a state. Eilam must be the name of a state because shushan ha-birah, which means Shushan the palace, was located in it. On the other hand, king of Goyim may be rendered as king of nations, Scripture not stating their names. The meaning of the verse is that Tidal was king over nations other than Shinar, Elasar and Eilam.
All these came as allies. Chaveru (came as allies) is in the kal.

The vale of siddim. Sidim means the same as sid (plaster) in and plaster them with plaster (ba-sid) (Devarim 27:2) and sad (plaster) in Thou puttest my feet also in the plaster (ba-sad) (Iyov 13:27). Sad, siddim, is like pat (morsel of bread), pittim.

Vale. The word vale is to be understood as if written twice. It is like the word al (not) in O Lord, rebuke me not (al) in Thine anger; Neither (ve-al) chasten me in Thy wrath (Tehillim 6:2). Our verse should be read as follows: All these came as allies unto the vale of Sidim, the same is the vale of the Salt Sea.

[And in the thirteenth year they rebelled.] U-shelosh esreh (and the thirteenth) should be interpreted u-ve-shelosh esreh (and in the thirteenth). It is similar to the word sheshet (six) in for in six (sheshet) days Hashem made the heaven and earth (Shemot 20:11). However, the author of the Seder Olam did not interpret it this way. He combined the years mentioned in our verse. His mind was greater than ours.
The Refaim. They were called Refaim (ghosts) because their appearance was so terrifying that whoever saw them died and was considered to be one of the Refaim, one of the dead.
The Eimim. They were so called because they were frightening.
In their Mount Seir. Be-hareram (in their mount) is in the pi’el. Its meaning is: when they went up to Mount Seir. It is like the word be-dabberam (when they spoke) (Shemot 7:7).
Against chedorlaomer. With Kedorlaomer.
Pits. Be’er (pit) in the Bible means a bubbling well. Its (pits) vocalization is exceptional because it is in the construct.
And they fell there. They deliberately fell there, in their desire to escape. And when Moshe heard it, he fell upon his face (Bamidbar 16:4) is similar.
Fled to the mountain. The phrase herah nasu is to be rendered: fled to the mountain. The word herah (to the mountain) is an irregular form.
Who dwelt in Sedom. Lot was dwelling in Sedom on that day.

[And there came one that had escaped.] Palit (one that had escaped) refers to a Sodomite who escaped and saved himself. Palit in one that had escaped (palit) out of Yerushalayim came unto me (Yechezkel 33:21) is similar. There is a Midrashic interpretation concerning the escapee.

He led forth his trained men. He armed them. Compare, ve-harek (arm) in, Arm (ve-harek) with the spear (Tehillim 35:3). Others say that va-yarek refers to the unsheathing of the sword. Compare, They empty themselves (yariku) upon the earth (Kohelet 11:3), and emptied (merikim) their sacks (Bereshit 42:35). A spear also has a sheath.

His trained men. Avraham had trained them many times for battle. This is the meaning of the term chanikhav (his trained men) even though Scripture does not previously note that Avraham trained young men for war. Those who identify Avraham’s trained men with his servant Eliezer on the basis of the numerical value of the latter’s name are indulging in Midrash, as Scripture does not speak in gematria (numericals). With this type of interpretation one can interpret any name as he wishes, both in a positive and a negative manner. Eliezer is to be taken literally.
And Malki-Tzedek. He was so called because he was king (melech) over a righteous (tzedek) place. Some identify Malki-Tzedek with Shem.
Shalem. This is Yerushalayim. In Shalem also is set His tabernacle, And His dwelling place in Tziyon (Tehillim 76:3) is proof of this.

And he was priest. This is be rendered as Onkelos does. Similarly, every time the word “priest” (kohen) is found in Scripture. That they may minister unto Me (ve-khihanu li) (Shemot 28:41) is proof of this. The meaning of al divrati Malkitzedek (after the manner of Malki-Tzedek) (Tehillim 110:4) will be found in my commentary on Psalms. Malki-Tzedek spoke properly and did the right thing in first blessing Avraham because he volunteered to rescue the captives. He then blessed Hashem for aiding Avraham and delivering Avraham’s adversaries into his hands.

Hath delivered. Miggen (hath delivered) means handed over. Temaggeneka (will she bestow on thee) in A crown of glory will she bestow on thee (temaggeneka) (Mishlei 4:9) is similar. The mem of miggen is a root letter. Avraham gave a tithe out of respect for Hashem. He found no one worthier than Malki-Tzedek to bestow his tithe on.
I have lifted up my hand. This indicates an oath. It is like, For I lift up my hand to heaven, etc. (Devarim 32:40).
[God Most High.] For behold, I have used the same name for God in my oath as this priest (Malki-Tzedek) when he blessed me.
That I will not take a thread. That with which garments are sewn.
A shoe-latchet. A strap used to tie a shoe.
Save only. Save only that which the young men took. This refers to what Avraham’s servants ate.
In a vision. A prophetic vision.
[I am thy shield.] I was your shield and saved you from the kings. I will also reward you because, of your own free will, leading a small force and relying on Me, you saved your nephew.

[Childless.] The yod of ariri (childless) is like the yod of achzari (cruel). The yod is dropped in the plural. Compare, they shall be childless (aririm) (Vayikra 20:21). Its meaning is as Onkelos explains it.

He that shall be possessor of my house. Meshek (possessor of) follows the paradigm of meches (levy) (Bamidbar 31:28). It has a root whose second and third letters are identical. It comes from the same root as shokek (leap) in leap upon it (Is. 33:4). It means the same as the word devek (glue) and is also vocalized with a segol. The word ben is to be read as if written twice. The verse is to read as follows: and he that shall be possessor of my house (ben meshek beti) is Eliezer, a native of Damesek (ben damesek Eliezer).
Of thy own bowels. A euphemism for the sexual organ. Bowels is used as a euphemism because the male member is close to them.
Righteousness. Compare, And it shall be righteousness unto us (Devarim 6:25). Tzedakah (righteousness) is a synonym for justice. However, in Rabbinic literature tzedakah has a different meaning.

That brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees. This verse proves what I have earlier noted, that God’s command to Avraham, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, etc., was given in Ur of the Chaldees, not in Charan.

Avraham had complete faith in Hashem’s word that he would beget a son who would be his heir. It was only with regard to the possession of the land that he asked for a sign. He acted like Gidon. Furthermore, all prophecies are conditional. Hashem’s oaths, on the other hand, are unconditional. Hence Avraham did not sin in requesting that a covenant be made between Hashem and himself.
A she-goat of three years old. Some render ez meshuleshet as three she-goats. However, it appears to me that the correct translation of the phrase is: a she-goat three years old.
And a ram. A full grown male sheep.
And a young pigeon. Gozal is a young dove. It is to be rendered this way because burnt offerings and other sacrifices were brought only from among the animals and birds mentioned here.

And divided them in the midst. He cut them up and separated the pieces. Bater (split) in Upon the split mountains (hare bater) (Cant. 2:17) and betarav (parts of) in between the parts thereof (betarav) (Yirmiyahu 34:18) are analogous to va-yevater (and divided them).

And laid each half over against the other. Note that the word ish (each) means the same as ba’al, which means the thing itself. Similarly, ish (man) in The Lord is a man (ish) of war; (Shemot 15:3); and ish (man) in the man (ve-ha-ish) Gabriel (Daniel 9:21); and ish (fellow) in a base fellow (ish beliyya’al) (Shmuel II 20:1). In the latter verse it is in the construct. Ish is also used in reference to the living creatures seen by Yechezkel, and to the curtains of the Tabernacle, viz., Five curtains shall be coupled together one (ishah) to another (Shemot 26:3). The meaning of our clause is that he placed the piece of each one (ish) over against its counterpart. The term ish is to be so interpreted because man and beast are two different beings.
But the birds divided he not. The turtle dove and the young dove. Tzippor (birds) is a general term.
The birds of prey. Ayit (birds of prey) is a type of bird. Ayit (bird of prey) in Is my heritage unto Me as a speckled bird of prey (ha-ayit) (Yirmiyahu 12:9) is similar.
Upon the carcasses. On the lifeless bodies.

And Avram drove them away. Va-yashev (drove away) has a dagesh in the shin to make up for a missing nun. He drove them and sent them off the carcasses. Yashev (he caused to blow) in He causeth His wind to blow (yashev rucho) (Tehillim 147:18) is similar. On the other hand, he may have flapped at the carcasses to drive the bird of prey off them.
And it came to pass, that, when the sun was going down. This clause indicates that Avraham took him all these (v. 10) during the day after he awoke from his prophetic vision.

That thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs. In Hebrew a person who has a family is likened to a branch attached to its source. Therefore such an individual is called an ezrach, for the meaning of ezrach is a branch, as in a sprouting tree with many branches (ke-ezrach ra’anan) (Tehillim 37:35). On the other hand, a stranger is termed ger in Hebrew from the word gargir (berry), for he is like a berry plucked from a branch. There are some unintelligent people who find this explanation farfetched. However, if they knew the meaning of each letter and its form then they would recognize the truth.
Four hundred years. Until the end of this period (four hundred years) starting from this very day.
Whom they shall serve. Whose slaves they shall be.
But thou shalt go to thy fathers. A euphemism for a natural death.
[In peace.] Unlike your enslaved descendants, you will die in dignity.

And in the fourth generation they shall come back hither. Many of the commentaries misunderstood the meaning of the word dor (generation). The sages of the Talmud said there were ten generations from Adam to Noach. We also find, to a thousand generations (Devarim 7:9) and Iyov speaks of four generations (Iyov 42:16). In my opinion the meaning of dor (generation) is dwells. Compare dur (dwell) in Than to dwell (mi-dur) in the tents of wickedness (Tehillim 84:11). A generation is measured by a person’s life span. Some are long and some are short. Our verse refers to the fourth generation starting from the first that lived as strangers in Mitzrayim. Thus it is written, thou shalt not abhor a Mitzri, because thou wast a stranger in his land (Devarim 23:8). And so it was: Kehat, Amram, Moshe and Aharon were strangers in Mitzrayim. Their children, who were the fourth generation, returned to the land of Kenaan.

For the iniquity of the Emori is not yet full. I have explained the meaning of iniquity in my comments on My punishment is greater than I can bear (Bereshit 4:13). The Emori are singled out because they were the most powerful of the Kenaani peoples. Behold, the great kings whom Moshe slew were Emori. Furthermore, it was five Emori kings who united to fight Yehoshua. There are other proofs. Similarly the prophet says concerning the Emori, Whose height was like the height of the cedars, And he was strong as the oaks (Am. 2:9). Whoever says that Emori (Emori) comes from the same root as amar (saying) does not contribute anything.
And it came to pass, that when the sun went down. Until now the sun had not yet set. It is similarly written, when the sun was about to go down (v. 12).

Thick darkness. Alatah (thick darkness) means darkness. The word alatah is also found in Yechezkel (12:6, 7, 12). It means a cloudy night. It might also refer to the darkness that sets in as soon as the last light has disappeared in the clouds.
Behold a smoking furnace, and a flaming torch. An image of a smoking furnace with a flaming torch in it.

Between these pieces. Ben ha-gezarim means between the pieces. This was the actual taking of the oath. The words of the covenant which they made before Me, when they cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof (Yirmiyahu 34:18) is similar. We thus read in the next verse, In that day Hashem made a covenant with Avram, saying, ‘Unto thy seed have I given this land,’ etc.
From the river of Mitzrayim. This refers to the Shichor, and not the Yeor.
The Keini, and the kenizzite and the Kadmonite. These are children of Kenaan. Each one had two names.

And the Refaim. This is what That also is accounted a land of Refaim (Devarim 2:20) refers to. Do not be surprised that Scripture lists the Kenaani and after him the Yevusi.
