However, the Gaon seems to have forgotten that the Bible relates, and (Yaakov) bowed himself to the ground seven times until he came near to his brother (Esav) (Bereshit 33:3). It appears to me that the prophet’s blessing was akin to a prayer, and Hashem accepted his prayer, for Yitzchak’s prayer was mainly concerned with the offspring of Yaakov and Esav. Those who have as yet not awakened from their foolish sleep think that we are in the exile of the Edomim (Esav). However, this is not so. Edom (Esav) was subject to Yehudah. Scripture thus states, In his (Yehoram’s) days Edom revolted from under the hand of Yehudah (Melachim II 8:20). We are also told that Yoav cut off every male in Edom (Melachim I 11:16). It is because of their subjugation to Yehudah that they rejoiced on the day of Yehudah’s calamity and told the Babylonians, Raze it, raze it even to the foundations thereof (Tehillim 137:7). The taunts of the Edomim on the day of Yerushalayim’s fall was harder for the Yehudim to bear than the afflictions visited upon them by the Babylonians. This is also the meaning of Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom (Eichah 4:21), and Neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Yehudah in the day of their destruction (Ovadyah 1:12). Also, Hyrcanus the elder made the Edomim (Esav’s descendants) guard Yerushalayim and had them circumcised. Also, in the days of Agrippa when Yerushalayim was taken, troops of Edomim came to Yehudah’s aid. The Romans who exiled us are from the seed of Kitim. Onkelos similarly explains Kitim to mean Rome in But ships shall come from the coast of Kitim (Bamidbar 24:24). The Kitim are the very kingdom of the Greeks as I have explained in my commentary on the Book of Daniel. [At first there were only a few people who believed in the man that was made into a god. The Romans accepted the belief in this man in the days of Constantine who introduced this new religion to the Romans upon the advice of an Edomi priest and placed upon his flag an image of this man. At that time there was no one in the world aside from a small group of Edomim who followed the new religion. ] Similarly the contemporary inhabitants of Mitzrayim, Sheva and the land of Eilam are called Yishmeelim even though only a tiny minority of the people living there are true decendants of the Yishmeelim.
And Esav hated. Va-yistom (and he hated) is to be rendered: and he harbored hatred. Va-yistemuhu (and hated him) (Bereshit 49:23) is similar.
And Esav said in his heart. It is possible that Esav confided this thought to one of his friends. Others say that Rivkah knew this through prophecy. The first interpretation appears correct.

Doth comfort himself. Mitnachem (doth comfort himself) comes from the same root as nechamah (consolation). The meaning of our clause is: Esav’s sole consolation is that he will be able to kill you. However, the Gaon says that mitnachem means to set a time and is similar in meaning to the Arabic wa’ad.

A few days. Yamim achadim (a few days) is to be translated as a few years. Compare yamim in for a full year (yamim) shall he have the right of redemption (Vayikra 25:29). Achadim (a few) means less than ten.
Why should I be bereaved. Rivkah was anxious lest they kill each other, or that Esav would be killed for murdering Yaakov. There is a Midrashic opinion that both Yaakov and Esav died in one day.

I am weary of my life. Katzti (I am weary) has the same meaning as tzakti (I am distressed). Compare U-nekitzennah (and vex it) in Let us go up against Yehudah and vex it (u-nekitzennah) (Is. 7:6). Scripture similarly says, the land whose two kings thou hast cast a horror of (katz) shall be foresaken (Is. 7:16).

[So Esav went unto Yishmael.] When Esav learned that Yitzchak blessed Yaakov a second time and charged him not to take a wife of the daughters of Kenaan, he went unto his uncle Yishmael and married his daughter Basmat, who was also called Machalat. She, like Yitro, had two names, for I believe that Yitro and Chovav are one and the same person.
The sister of nebaioth. He was the most important of all his brothers. It is also possible that Yishmael had many wives and that Machalat was Nabaioth’s sister from the same mother.

[And Yaakov went out from beer-sheba.] Saadiah Gaon is of the opinion that va-yelekh charanah (and went toward Charan) is to be interpreted as, to go to Charan. However, this is not so. Va-yelekh charanah is to be interpreted literally. After telling us that Yaakov left Beer Sheva and went to Charan, Scripture returns and tells us what he encountered on the way to Charan. Yaakov did not arrive in Charan on the day he left Beer Sheva, because Scripture explicitly tells us that he spent a night on the way.

[And he lighted upon the place.] The reason the bet of ba-makom (the place) is vocalized with a pattach is that Moshe in writing the Torah did so in order to indicate the place that was well known in his time. Similarly the prophet Hoshea said, And there (at Beit El) he would speak with us (Hoshea 12:5). Hoshea said this because he prophesied in Beit El concerning Yerovam the son of Yoash. Hoshea used the term “with us” because Amos, too, prophesied in Beit El. It is clear from the Book of Amos that Beit El was a holy place. According to the plain meaning of the text, va-yifga (and he lighted) is not to be translated as, and he prayed, as in neither make intercession (tifga) to Me (Yirmiyahu 7:16), because we never find in the entire Bible the word makom (place) meaning Hashem. Do not pay any attention to the Midrashic interpretation that explains makom, in makom acher (Es. 4:14), as referring to Hashem, because it most certainly does not. Proof of this is found in the word acher (another) which follows makom.
Of the stones of the place. Its meaning is: one of the stones of the place.

Under his head. Me-ra’ashotav (under his head) is a plural. It is similar to margelotav (his feet) (Rut 3:4; 14). It is surprising that Rabbi Shmuel Ben Hofni confused the dreams of common men with prophetic dreams.

[And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth.] Those who say that the ladder seen by Yaakov refers to a statue, or that it refers to Sinai because it is numerically equivalent to it, are indulging in Midrash. Rabbi Shlomo ibn Gabirol, the Spaniard, says that Yaakov’s “ladder” alludes to man’s heavenly soul, and that “the angels of God” signify thoughts of wisdom. Rabbi Yehoshua explains the dream of the ladder to mean that Yaakov’s prayers ascended the Heavens via the ladder and in response to his supplications salvation was sent down to him. These commentators have apparently not studied the prophecies of Zecharyah, Amos and Yirmiyahu. The way to interpret Yaakov’s dream is to view it as a parable. It teaches that nothing is hidden from God and that what happens below is contingent on the decree from above. There is thus, as it were, a ladder linking heaven and earth by which angels ascend to inform God what they have seen on earth after going over it. Scripture also states that other angels come down to fulfill God’s commands. The imagery presented is that of a king and his servants.
And thou shalt spread abroad. U-faratzta (and thou shalt spread abroad) is to be rendered: and thou shalt multiply. Va-yifrotz ha-ish (and the man increased) is similar (Bereshit 30:43).
Surely Hashem is in this place. The meaning of Yaakov’s statement is that there are places where miracles are seen. I cannot explain why this is so because it is a deep mystery.

This is none other than the House of Elokim. This is a chosen place where a man in time of need will pray and his supplications will be accepted. Many ask, how could Yaakov set up a pillar? However, they have forgotten that Moshe set up twelve pillars. Scripture does not prohibit a pillar set up to honor the Lord. Scripture merely states, Neither shalt thou set thee up a pillar, which the Lord thy Elokim hateth (Devarim 16:22). I will explain the latter verse when I come to it.
And poured oil upon the top of it. So that he would recognize it when he returned.

[Then shall Hashem be my Elokim.] Hashem that shall be my Elokim is the One known by the Tetragrammaton. Scripture clearly states, And, behold Hashem (spelled with the tetragramaton) stood beside him (v. 13). You will find an explanation of this name of Elokim in my comments on the first Torah portion of Exodus.

[God’s house.] The meaning of shall be God’s House is: it will be a fixed place for my prayers and for my tithing; for out of all the money that thou shalt give me, I will give a tithe out of respect for God to one who is fit to receive it. Those who say that the tithe refers to Levi are indulging in Midrash. This is so because we do not find anywhere in the Torah that a man shall tithe his children. The only tithes that we find in the Pentateuch are cattle, sheep and produce.

And he looked. Va-yar (and he looked) is an irregular form, for though a kal, its yod is vocalized with a pattach notwithstanding the fact that it is not followed by a guttural, in which case the preceding letter is normally vocalized with a pattach. Furthermore, this form (va-yar) cannot drop the conversive vav nor come with any conjugational prefix but the yod. I believe that when one wants to conjugate the root resh, alef, heh in the third person according to the paradigm of va-yishb in and took some of them captive (va-yishb) (Bamidbar 21:1), the heh would be dropped and the alef unsounded. Nevertheless, the chirik would remain beneath the yod. The word would thus be pronounced va-yir and it would follow the paradigm of va-yif (thus was it fair) in va-yif be-godlo (thus was it fair in its greatness) (Ez. 31:7) and would be thought to mean, and he threw, from the root yod, resh, heh (throw). To avoid this possibility our word (va-yar) is vocalized with a pattach beneath the yod.
And they rolled the stone. The shepherds rolled the stone.

Whence. Me-ayin (whence) means what place are you from. The word ayin without the mem prefixed to it could not be used for whence, for ayin means nothing. Nevertheless, we find the word me-ayin also used for nothing, as in Behold, ye are nothing (me-ayin) (Is. 41:24).
And, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh. The accent is on the last syllable in the word ba’ah (cometh) because it is a participle. It is similar to words in the po’el form.
Rachel came. Ba’ah (came) is pentultimately accented. It is a verb in the perfect.

And Yaakov told Rachel. And Yaakov told Rachel should have been written before And Yaakov kissed Rachel (v. 11). Its meaning is: And Yaakov had already told Rachel that he was her father’s brother before he kissed her. There are many such instances in Scripture.
All these things. The account of the blessings.
The space of a month. I have already explained the meaning of chodesh yamin (the space of a month).
Thy wages. Maskurtekha (thy wages) follows the paradigm of matkonet in And the tale (matkonet) of the bricks (Shemot 5:8).

Weak. Rakkot is to be taken literally. Some ask, why were Leah’s eyes weak? They raise this question because they believe Hashem’s thoughts are like their thoughts, and they think that all people have to be formed alike. Ben Efraim said that an alef is missing in the word rakkot (weak), its meaning being arukhot (long). However, Ben Efraim himself was missing an alef.

Of beautiful form. To’ar (form) is similar to ta’ar (drawn) in And the border was drawn (ve-ta’ar) (Jos. 15:9). The meaning of beautiful form is that each organ of her body such as her nose and mouth were beautifully drawn (formed).
[And fair to look upon.] Her whole body was fair to look upon, or And fair to look upon refers to the complexion of her face.
And Yaakov served seven years for Rachel. Be-rachel (for Rachel) should be rendered because of Rachel.
Fulfill the week of this one. The seven days of the marriage feast. Zot (this one) refers to Leah.
Will love me. Ye’ehavani (will love me) is vocalized with a pattach beneath the bet. It is similar to tidbakani (overtake me) in lest the evil overtake me (tidbakani) (Bereshit 19:19).
Will my husband be joined unto me. Yillaveh (will be joined) is similar to ve-nilvu (and they shall be joined) in And they shall be joined (ve-nilvu) unto thee (Bamidbar 18:4).

This time will I praise Hashem. Ha-pa’am should be explained as if written ha-pa’am ha-zot (this time). Its meaning is, now that I have four sons I will give thanks to Hashem for I will not desire any more children. One can paraphrase This time will I praise Hashem by: I will praise Hashem because he has given me all this and has satisfied me. Therefore she left off bearing.
Give me children. Pray to God as your father did.
Am I in Elokim’s stead. Am I in Hashem’s place. It is possible that Yaakov prayed on behalf of Rachel but the time for the acceptance of his prayer on her behalf had not yet arrived.
And I also may be builded up. I have explained the word ve-ibbaneh (and I also may be builded up) in my comments on Sarah’s use of the same term.
Judged me. The second nun of dananni (judged me) has a dagesh to compensate for a missing suffixal nun.

Wrestlings. Naftule (wrestlings) is a noun in the nifal. Its meaning is I strove, as a man who, when wrestling with another, twists (yiftol) in his effort to overpower his opponent in order to throw him to the ground. The word tittappal (Thou dost deal tortuously) (Shmuel II 22:27) is similar. The reason Rachel mentioned Elokim, (naftule Elokim), is either that out of respect for Hashem she had given her handmaiden to her husband, or that Elokim helped her in her struggle.
Fortune is come. Bagad (fortune is come) is really two words with the alef missing. Similarly, bavel. Also, bamah as is clearly explained in Yechezkel (20:29).

The meaning of Gad is a troop. Leah said this because she now had a “troop” of sons. Others say that gad means good fortune as in the Arabic; and that prepare a table for Fortune (gad) (Is. 65:11), with the latter meaning Jupiter, is similar. Actually, however, gad in the latter verse refers to the troops of heaven.
Happy am I. Be-oshri means, on account of my happiness.

Mandrakes. Onkelos renders dudaim yavruchin (Aramaic for mandrakes). They are similarly called in Arabic. Mandrakes give off a pleasant scent. Thus it is written, The mandrakes give forth fragrance (Cant. 7:14). The mandrakes are shaped like humans. They have the shape of a head and hands. I do not know how they can help a woman conceive since their nature is cold.
For thy son’s mandrakes. Tachet (for) is to be rendered: in place of and as a reward for.
Elokim hath endowed me. The meaning of zevadani (hath endowed me) is: has given me a portion. The word zevadani is not found elsewhere in Scripture.

Will dwell with me. Yizbeleni means will dwell with me; i.e., his dwelling (zevulo) will always be with me. Compare, I have surely built Thee a house of habitation (bet zevul) (Melachim I 8:13). Yetza’uni (are gone forth from me), in banai yetza’uni (my children are gone from me) (Yirmiyahu 10:20), and vi-yevo’uni (also come unto me) (Tehillim 119:41) are similar. All of these are intransitive verbs with the pronominal suffix ni.
And afterwards she bore a daughter. Some say that Dinah was Zevulun’s twin.

God hath taken away my reproach. Asaf (taken away) is to be rendered cut off. Compare, And gladness and joy are taken away (ve-ne’esaf) (Is. 16:10). Others interpret what Rachel said as, God saw the insults which the women hurled at me because I was barren and by giving me a son He, as it were, gathered (asaf) and collected the insults. It is clear from Scripture that Yaakov’s twelve children were born in seven years. When the ancients numbered them they could only explain how this was possible by saying that each was born six months and some days after conception. However, this was not necessarily so. It is posssible that Leah gave her handmaiden to Yaakov before Naftali was born, that Rachel conceived before the birth of Zevulun, and that we do not know when Dinah was born.
For whom I have served thee. This refers to my wives, not my children. It is similar to and shed the blood of war in peace (Melachim I 2:5).
I have observed the signs. Nichashti (I have observed the signs) means I have divined, for Lavan was an enchanter and had teraphim.

Appoint. Nokvah (appoint) is an imperative. It follows the paradigm of zokhrah (remember) in Remember (zokhrah) me, O my Elokim, for good (Nechemyah 13:31). The meaning of nokvah (appoint) is, clearly state, as we see from Which the mouth of Hashem shall mark out (yikkovennu) (Is. 62:2). The dagesh of yikkovennu (shall mark out) compensates for the missing nun. We find the same with the word yiddevennu (make them willing) in whose heart maketh him willing (yiddevennu) (Shemot 25:2).

Withersoever I turned. Le-ragli (withersoever I turned) is to be rendered: because of my foot. It is the custom of people to say so and so has a good foot. What Yaakov was saying was: you have been blessed ever since I came to your house. The heh of me’umah (aught in v. 31) is superfluous. The word is also found spelled without the heh.
Streaked. The streak was on the animal’s foot. Akuddim (streaked) refers to a cord-like mark that bound the foot
Speckled. Nekuddim means speckled.
Grizzled. Beruddim (grizzled) comes from the same root as barad (hail). It means having white spots.

[Spotted.] Talu is a general term for all type of spots. It comes from the same root as u-metulla’ot (and clouted) in and worn shoes and clouted (u-metulla’ot) upon their feet (Yehoshua 9:5). The meaning of u-metulla’ot is marked. The term seh (v. 32), refers to he-goats. It is similarly written the sheep (seh kevasim) and the goat (seh izim) (Devarim 14:4). Now since talu (spotted) is a general term for all type of spots, the meaning of every speckled and spotted (talu) one is: every he-goat speckled, streaked and grizzled.
And every dark one among the sheep. Chum means black. It is possible that chum means black because it is affected by heat (chom), for a black object gets hotter than a white object.
And the spotted and speckled among the goats. Streaked, grizzled and speckled.
Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats. Speckled, grizzled and streaked.
Among the goats. He and she-goats.
And he removed that day the he-goats that were streaked and spotted. Spotted (telu’im) means speckled and grizzled.
[And all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted.] The interpretation of telu’ot (spotted) is streaked and grizzled. This is what Scripture means by everyone that had white in it.

And all the dark ones among the sheep. The black sheep. Chum (dark, black) is an adjective similar to a pa’ul. It follows the paradigm of sug (dissembler) in The dissembler (sug) in heart (Mishlei 14:14). A great grammarian explained the word haser (removing) in removing (haser) from thence (v. 32) as an infinitive, meaning to remove. The meaning of the aforementioned verse according to this scholar is: I will pass through all thy flock today to remove from thence every…and that which I remove will be my hire. He further explained And gave them into the hands of his sons (v. 35) as referring to Yaakov’s sons. However, he said that he set three days journey betwixt himself and Yaakov (v. 36) pertains to Lavan. This comment is wrong in view of the fact that Yaakov had no son older than Reuven, and he was not yet seven years old. This is the way our passage is to be explained: haser (v. 32) is, as its form indicates, an imperative meaning “remove” and the meaning of and of such shall be my hire (v. 32) is: such as these which you now remove will in the future be my hire.

So shall my righteousness witness against me. My righteousness shall testify for me before thee, when you come and look over my hire, viz., the flock that I have separated for myself. If you find among the latter a he and she-goat that is not streaked, speckled and grizzled or a sheep that is not black, then it shall be counted stolen. Behold you have already removed from the flock all goats streaked, speckled and grizzled and all black sheep.
And Lavan said: behold. Hen (behold) is identical in meaning to hinneh, the heh being superfluous. It is similar in this regard to ha-eleh (these) and ha-el (these).
And he removed. Lavan removed.
And he set. Here, too, Scripture speaks of Lavan.
Rods of. Makkal (rods of) is vocalized with a pattach because it is in the construct.

Poplar…almond…and plane tree. Livneh (poplar), luz (almond) and armon (plane tree) are names of trees. However, lach (fresh) is an adjective. Saadiah Gaon says that luz means almond since that is its meaning in Arabic, and Arabic, Hebrew and Aramaic belong to the same family.
Making the white appear. He peeled the bark. Compare, Hashem hath made bare (chasaf) His holy arm (Is. 52:10).
Peeled. The word pitzel (peeled) means he made small cuts.
In the gutters. Pools containing water for the sheep to drink from.

And they conceived. Va-yechamnah (and they conceived) is a combination of masculine and feminine forms. We find the same in the word va-yisharnah (and took…the straight way) in And the kine took the straightway (va-yisharnah) (Shmuel I 6:12).

And the flocks conceived. Va-yechemu means: and they conceived. This word is irregularly vocalized because of the chet which is a guttural. It should have been vocalized as va-yeshevu (and they sat down) in And they sat down (va-yeshevu) to eat bread (Bereshit 37:25). Don’t be surprised at Scripture’s use of the masculine when referring to female sheep. Hebrew is strict in differentiating between the masculine and feminine forms only in the singular and not in the plural.

At the sight of the rods. El ha-maklot should be rendered at the sight of the rod. Many are amazed at what is reported in our verse and say that it can only be described as an out of the ordinary phenomenon. Really, what Scripture describes is indeed one of the wonders of nature. However, it is a natural law. Even a woman who is created in the image of the angels affects her fetus by what she looks at while she is pregnant.
And spotted. Grizzled. This is so because telu’im (spotted) is a general term for all types of spots.

And Yaakov separated the lambs. Yaakov also did one more thing. He separated the lambs and chose the streaked and the dark ones and set the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and dark ones so that they would produce similar offspring. This resulted in his having his own droves which he did not put unto Lavan’s flock. Others say that Yaakov separated the lambs from his own flock and that and put his own droves apart should have preceded and Yaakov separated the lambs.
Whensoever the stronger of the flock did conceive. In the month of Nisan, so that all those born would be strong and healthy.
But when the flock were feeble. In the month of Tishrei. Yaakov did this so that Lavan would not know that he was employing the sticks to produce spotted goats.
Feeble. Atufim means feeble; compare, Their soul fainted (titattaf) in them (Tehillim 107:5).
The words of Lavan’s sons. Lavan had sons as Scripture explicitly tells us, and (Lavan) gave them into the hand of his sons (Bereshit 30:35).

Your father’s countenance. I can tell by looking at your father’s countenance that he is not (ennenu) toward me as beforetime. On the other hand, enennu (he is not) may refer to countenance (pene). Compare, The anger (pene) of Hashem hath divided them (chillekam) (Eichah 4:16).

Hath mocked me. Hetel is irregular in that it lacks a dagesh. It should have a dagesh like the word va-yehattel (and he mocked) in that Eliyahu mocked (va-yehattel) them (Melachim I 18:27). The meaning of hetel is mocked.

Ten times. The word monin (times) is akin to the word meneh (number) in Go number (meneh) the people (Shmuel II 24:1). The meaning of our verse is: your father deceived me ten times. Or ten signifies many times.

From the statement, The streaked shall be thy wages, it is clear that Lavan changed Yaakov’s hire so that it was limited only to streaked goats. At other times Lavan limited Yaakov’s hire to speckled goats.

Thus Elokim hath taken away. Va-yatzel (hath taken away) is similar in meaning to va-yenatzelu (and they despoiled) in And they despoiled (va-yenatzelu) the Mitzrim (Shemot 12:36). Both (va-yatzel and va-yenatzelu) come from the same root as hatzileni (deliver me) (Bereshit 32:12), although in the latter case the meaning of the word is a bit different from the first two examples. What Yaakov told his wives was also true. Yaakov dreamed that Hashem would aid him so that his sheep would increase and be strong even without the use of the peeled sticks.

I am the God of Beit El. Its meaning is: I am the God, God of Beit El. The same is the case with and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Bereshit 2:9), which is to be interpreted as if written: and the tree of the knowledge, knowledge of good and evil.

For he hath sold us. It is as if he sold us in that he did not do with us what a father normally does with his daughters. What he did was to say to you, “Guard my flock and take my daughters as your hire.”
He had gathered. Rakhash (he had gathered) comes from the same root as rekhush (substance).

Now Lavan was gone to shear his sheep. That were in the care of his sons who were three days journey away, as is reported by Scripture (Bereshit 30:35, 36). Hence, it was told Lavan on the third day that Yaakov was fled (v. 22).

The teraphim. Some say that the teraphim are copper objects used to tell time. Others say that astrologers have the power to make an image that speaks at certain times. They offer proof from For the teraphim have spoken vanity (Zecharyah 10:2). However, this is not the meaning of the aforementioned verse. I believe that the teraphim are human images made to draw power from above. I am not permitted to explain this any further. Proof that the teraphim are human forms can be found in the teraphim which Michal, the daughter of Shaul, placed in David’s bed thereby fooling the guards into thinking that the teraphim were really David. As to the verse which states, For the children of Yisrael shall sit solitary many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without pillar, and without ephod or teraphim (Hoshea 3:4), it can be explained in two ways. One, the prophet says, Yisrael shall be without king, and without prince because Elokim chose only members of the Davidic family to be kings over Yisrael. Therefore the verse which follows says, afterward shall the children of Yisrael return, and seek Hashem their Elokim, and David their king (v. 5). The verse continues, and without sacrifice, and without pillar; this refers to sacrifices and pillars to the idols. In a similar manner, and without ephod also refers to idolatry, because the worshippers of Ba'al made an imitation of the ephod that Moshe made. Hence Scripture reads ephod and not “the ephod” as in Bring hither the ephod (Shmuel I 23:9). Therefore an ephod in his hand (Ibid. v. 6) does not refer to the ephod made by Moshe. I will explain the ephod and offer irrefutable proofs for my interpretation concerning it in the proper place if Elokim will be kind to me and grant me life. The second interpretation is that and without ephod or teraphim means, they will neither serve Elokim (without ephod) nor idols (or teraphim). That teraphim are idols can be ascertained by Lavan’s referring to them as gods (v. 30). Some say that Rachel stole the teraphim in order to keep her father from idolatry. If this were the case, why did she take them with her and not bury them on the way? The most likely reason that Rachel stole the teraphim was that Lavan, her father, was an astrologer, and Rachel feared that he would look at the stars and discover which way they fled.
And Yaakov outwitted Lavan. Yaakov stole nothing from Lavan save his “wits.” Scripture uses the term heart for wits because the heart is the seat of man’s intelligence.

And Elokim came to Lavan the Arami. This occurred before he overtook him (v. 23). Therefore its (v. 4) meaning is, and Elokim had already come to Lavan the Arami. I have already pointed out many similar instances. Hashem appeared to Lavan out of respect for Yaakov.
Either good or bad. Do not speak to Yaakov about returning even if you think it is for his good.
And Lavan with his brethren pitched. Et echav is to be rendered: with his brethren.

The word tent written in reference to Yaakov also carries over to Lavan. That is, now Yaakov had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Lavan pitched his tent with his brethren in the mountain of Gilad.
Now hast thou done foolishly. Aso (done) is an infinitive. It is in the construct with either this or so. However, they are missing.
It is in the power. El is to be rendered power. Compare, I am become as a man that hath no help (eyal) (Tehillim 88:5).
Longest. Nikhsof (longest) is an infinitive in the nifal. It is similar to nilchom (fight) in or did he ever fight (nilchom) against them (Jud. 11:25).
The word nikhsafta means thou longest. Yikhsof (eager) in He is like a lion that is eager (yikhsof) to tear in pieces (Tehillim 17:12) is similar.

He shall not live. Because I will put him to death. Some say that this was a prayer and it was because of this utterance that Rachel died on the way. If this be so, let them tell us who prayed and thus caused the death of Pinchas’ wife?

And Lavan went into Yaakov’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two maid-servants. Both maid-servants shared one tent. Or it (v. 33) means into the tent of each one of the two maid-servants. Afterward Lavan entered Leah’s tent a second time. Proof of this is Scripture’s statement, And he went out of Leah’s tent. It is also possible that Yaakov’s tent was between Leah’s and Rachel’s tents. However, it appears to me that the Bible tells us what happened in abridged form and puts off the mention of Rachel’s tent for last. The sequence of events was as follows. Lavan searched Yaakov’s tent, then Leah’s tent, then Rachel’s tent and then the tent of the two maid-servants. The meaning of our verses (33 and 34) is that Lavan searched Yaakov’s tent, Leah’s tent and the tent of the two maid-servants and found nothing because there was nothing of his there. Scripture then tells us that when Lavan went out of Leah’s tent and into Rachel’s tent where the teraphim had been, Rachel had by then taken them and put them in the saddle of the camel.

[In the saddle.] Some say that kar (saddle) is a kind of saddle cloth. However, I believe that the term kar ha-gamal (saddle of the camel) means a camel, as in Send ye the camel (kar) for the ruler of the land (Is. 16:1); and u-va-kirkarot (and upon the camels) (Is. 66:20). I further hold that the driver or rider of the kar (camel) is called the kari (Melachim II 11:19). Rachel took the teraphim and put them in the place where the camel (kar ha-gamal) was kept.
And sat upon them. She was not in the tent.
That thou hast hotly pursued. Dalakta means pursued. Yidlak in the poor is hotly pursued (yidlak) (Tehillim 10:2) is similar.
I bore the loss of it. If any of the flock was torn by beasts, I bore the guilt and I gave you its equivalent.

Stolen by day. The yod of genuveti (stolen) is superfluous. It is similar to the yod of mele’ati (full of) (Is. 1:21). The meaning of our verse is: whether stolen by day or by night, of my hand didst thou require it.
And the fear of Yitzchak. Yitzchak’s fear of Hashem aided me, for the merits of a father help his son.

[Empty.] The mem of rekam (empty) is not a root letter. The word is a noun. The Bible employs this form (rekam) with the masculine, feminine and the plural. The mems of omnam (verily, truly) and chinnam (for nothing, gratis) are similar.
And what can I do this day for these my daughters. Lavan was being especially explicit. The verse should be understood thus: and to these my daughters, what can I do to them?
A pillar. Because he set it up.
A heap. A gal (heap) is so called because it is formed by rolling stones together. He also called it Mitzpah.
[Hashem watch.] The meaning of yitzef adonai is : Hashem will watch. I have appointed thee a watchman (tzofeh) (Ez. 3:17) is similar.

[When we are absent.] Ki nissater (when we are absent) is to be read as if written: ki nissater anachnu. We will be distant one from another and will not be able to see each other. Nevertheless, Hashem will see each one of us.
[For he said.] This refers to Lavan. Yaakov called it Mitzpah because Lavan said to him, Hashem will watch, etc.

If thou shalt afflict my daughters. Saadiah Gaon explains this to mean: if you will not cohabit with your wives. Now this is a strange rendition of afflict. Nowhere in Scripture does afflict have this connotation. What problem is there in interpreting the term according to its plain sense? Its meaning is: do not do anything evil to my daughters or force them to do things against their will.Jagar-sahadutha is Aramaic for Galeed.

Which I have set up. Lavan and his brethren. They cast stones and formed the heap. Yariti comes from the same root as yarah (cast) in hath He cast (yarah) into the sea (Shemot 15:4). He cast them into one place.
That I will not pass over. The covenant made on this heap. E’evor (pass over) in our verse has the meaning of violate, as in they have transgressed (averu) the statute (Is. 24:5).
[For harm.] To do harm. Others say that it means, thou shalt not pass over this heap to harm me and I will not pass over this heap to harm thee.

[The Elokim of their father.] Each one said: the Elokim of our Father judge betwixt us. However, Yaakov referred to the Elokim of Avraham and Lavan to the god of Nachor, his grandfather who worshiped idols as is attested by Yehoshua.

And Yaakov swore by the fear of his father. Fear of his father means the One whom his father feared. Others say that this alludes to the day when Yaakov’s father Yitzchak was bound on the altar. The latter interpretation is not far-fetched.
His sons. His grandsons, the sons of his daughters.

And the angels of Elokim met him. To assist him on the way. Only Yaakov saw the camp of angels surrounding his camp. He called the name of the place Machanayim (two camps), because of the two camps there, his and the angels’.

And Yaakov sent. This verse teaches us that the land of Edom lies between Charan and the land of Yisrael. This disproves Saadiah Gaon’s contention that Sinai, Seir and Paran are next to each other. [MESSENGERS.] From among his servants.
Thus shall ye say unto my Lord. Yaakov used this language so that it would be clear to them that Esav was his lord and they should address him as a servant addresses his master.

And stayed until now. The alef of echar (and stayed) is a first person imperfect prefix. It is vocalized with a tzere to make up for the missing alef of the root. Ehav (I love) in I love them (ehav) that love me (Mishlei 8:17) is similar. The alef of the root is dropped because it is extremely difficult to pronounce two alefs back to back. Echar is a kal.
Oxen and asses. These are nouns referring to the respective species.
And I have sent to tell my Lord. That I wish to do whatever he commands me. This is the meaning of that I may find favor in thy sight
And moreover he cometh to meet thee. He was told that you are coming.

And was distressed. This thing distressed him. Va-yetzer (and he was distressed) is in the hifil. It is similar to ve-hetzar (and he shall besiege) in and he shall besiege (ve-hetzar) thee (Devarim 28:52).
And he divided. The yad of va-yachatz (and he divided) is vocalized with a pattach because it precedes a guttural. Compare, (va-ya’al) in And Moshe went up (va-ya’al moshe) (Shemot 19:20).
Camp. The word for camp (machaneh) can be either masculine or feminine like the word for house (bayit) and place (makom).

Then the camp which is left shall escape. Perhaps the camp that is left shall flee, or perhaps my brother’s anger shall be assuaged after smiting one of the camps, or perhaps Hashem will send them relief and deliverance. If the Aram be too strong for me, then thou shalt save me (Shmuel II 10:11) is similar. Rabbi Shlomo’s comment, to the effect that then the camp that is left shall escape means that the camp will be saved despite Esav’s intention, is Midrashic. Although Hashem promised Yaakov, And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth (Bereshit 28:14), Yaakov did not know whether it referred to the children he now had, or to children he would have in the future. A prophet does not know hidden things unless Hashem reveals them to him. Yaakov was alive when Yosef was sold into slavery and yet was unaware of it. Similarly Elisha said, and Hashem hath hid it from me (Melachim II 4:27). The above also answers those who ask, why was Yaakov afraid considering that Hashem promised that he would protect him, viz., Hashem’s assurance, and I will be with thee (Bereshit 31:3)? The latter is also the promise referred to by Yaakov when he said, And thou saidest I will surely do thee good (v. 13). Yaakov was afraid because of the possibility that he alone would escape. Furthermore, we know that the personality of the individual is taken into account when his sins are considered, be they major or minor transgressions. Therefore, a minor sin committed by a great personality is considered a major transgression. Yaakov was afraid that he may have sinned or inadvertently transgressed in his mind and as a result of this Hashem no longer would be with him. Do not be amazed at what I write, for behold, Moshe the greatest of men, whom Hashem himself sent to bring Yisrael out of Mitzrayim erred and Hashem sent an angel to kill him.

I am not worthy. Katonti (I am not worthy) is vocalized like yakholti (I have prevailed) in gam yakholti (Bereshit 30:8). The meaning of our verse is: I am insignificant and of little worth for you to have done all these merciful deeds for me. I have already explained the meaning of mercy and truth.

And smite me. And smite me applies to two phrases. It is similar to And Shaul’s son had two men that were captains of bands (Shmuel II 4:2). Our verse should be read as follows: and smite me and smite the mother and the children.
Two hundred she-goats. Yaakov sent ten females for every male of the flock, four bulls for each cow, and two she-asses for every foal. He did this because he knew their nature.

And put a space. The word revach means a space. Harevachah (respite) in That there was respite (harevachah) (Shemot 8:11) is close in meaning to it. The meaning of the latter is, there was a separation between one plague and the other. It is similar to ve-ravach (found relief) in so Shaul found relief (ve-ravach le-sha’ul) (Shmuel I 16:23).
And asketh thee saying. U-she’elekha (and asketh thee) is vocalized the same as ahevekha (he loveth thee).
And all that followed. Scripture says this because there were five groups.
When ye find him. The tzadi of be-motza’akhem (when ye find) is vocalized with a pattach because it precedes a guttural. This is so even though we do not find another example of this in the Bible.
For he said. He said in his heart. These are the words of Moshe.

[I will appease him.] Akhapperah (I will appease him) means I will cover or hide. Panav (him) means his anger. Peneha (her countenance) in and her countenance (u-faneha) was no more sad (Shmuel I 1:18) is similar.

And passed over the ford of the jabbok. Yaakov passed over first. He then returned and took his wives and children and brought them over the ford. Thus the meaning of and passed over is and he had already passed over. He then went back for a final look to see if anything was forgotten.
And there wrestled a man. Va-ye’avek (and there wrestled) comes from the same root as avak (dust). They struggled so that dust arose between them.

Until the breaking of the day. Ad alot ha-shachar (until the breaking of the day) means until the darkness of the night went away. Others say that shachar (dawn) refers to the image of light that appears in the clouds before sunrise. Shacher (light) in wherein there is no light (shacher) (Is. 8:20) is similar.
That he prevailed not against him. The angel against Yaakov.
He touched the hollow of his thigh. Yaakov’s thigh.
Was strained. Va-teka (was strained) is similar to teka (be moved) in Lest My soul be moved (teka) from thee (Yirmiyahu 6:8). The hollow of Yaakov’s thigh moved out of its place.

The sinew of the thigh-vein. The meaning of the term gid ha-nasheh (the sinew of the thigh-vein) is known from the tradition received and transmitted to us by the Talmudic sages. No one but those lacking in understanding and knowledge of nature have any doubt as to its definition. The latter interpret gid (sinew) to refer to the penis and hold that nassheh (thigh-vein) comes from the same root as nashim (women). Note, the angel that appeared to Yaakov was corporeal. This will be explained to you, if Hashem will enlighten you, in the chapter that begins, for My name is in him (Shemot 23:21).
[And Rachel and Yosef hindermost.] He placed Rachel and Yosef last so that they might possibly escape. Yaakov did this because of his great love for them.

[And kissed him.] The Midrashic interpretation concerning the dots on ve-yishakehu (and kissed him) is good for them that are drawn from the breasts. It is obvious from the plain meaning of the text that Esav did not intend to harm Yaakov, the proof being and they wept, as Yosef did with his brethren.
Who are these with thee. Mi eleh lakh can be interpreted as meaning who are these with thee, or who are these who are yours.
Graciously given. Chanan means gave graciously. Grant them graciously (channunu) unto us (Jud. 21:22) is similar. The word chinnam (gratuitously) comes from the same root.
What meanest thou. The word mi (what) always refers to a person. The meaning of our clause is: to whom did you send this gift, or whom were you thinking of when you sent this gift.
Nay, I pray thee. I pray my lord not to so speak. I have previously noted Rabbi Shmuel Ha-Nagid’s interpretation of the term al (nay).

As one seeth the face of Elokim. The face of an angel. Many of the commentators explain that the angel with whom Yaakov wrestled came to encourage him not to lose heart and fear Esav. For if an angel could not overcome him, certainly no human could. The word sarita (thou hast striven), in thou hast striven (sarita) with (im) Elokim (Bereshit 32:29), does not mean the same as va-yaser (was prince) in And Avimelech was prince (va-yasar) over (al) Yisrael (Jud. 9:22), because im (with) is not the same as al (over). Our phrase (Bereshit 32:29) means that you are considered a prince among the angels, and also among human princes. Some ask, what does Scripture mean by And the sun rose upon him (Bereshit 32:32) when the sun rises all over the world at the same time? This is a nonsensical question because the sun rises at different times in different places. For example, there is a difference of one and a third hours in sunrise and also twelve degrees in latitude between Yerushalayim and the place where I wrote this commentary, namely the city of Lucca. This thing is certain and beyond doubt. The meaning of tzole’a (and he limped) (Bereshit 32:32) is, he walked on one side. The meaning of al ken (therefore) (Bereshit 32:33) is, in commemoration of this thing.

Let us take our journey. Some say that nisah (let us take our journey) is an imperative. It is similar to shilchah (send) in Send (shilchah) the lad (Bereshit 43:8) and niflu (fall) in Fall (niflu) on us (Hoshea 10:8).

And let us go. All of us. And I will go before thee; i.e., I will not move away from you. However, it is possible that nisah is similar to va-nissse’ah (then we departed) in Then we departed (va-nisse’ah) from the river of Ahava (Ezra 8:31). The meaning of our verse thus is: Let us all take our journey, and I will go before thee.
The children are tender. The oldest was twelve years and some days old.

Giving suck. Alot (giving suck) is similar to alot (pregnant) in and gently leadeth those that are pregnant (alot) (Is. 40:11). It means pregnant cattle. They are called alot because the he-goats went up (alu) on them.
The meaning of alai (are a care to me) is that I have to care for them that no harm befall them.
And if they overdrive them. If the drivers overdrive them, then all the flock will die.
And I will journey on. This is to be understood as, and I will journey on with them.
Gently. The yod of le’itti (gently) is either superfluous or is a first person pronominal suffix.

According to the pace of the cattle. Because of the cattle, whose care is my work. I believe that the meaning of melakhah is what a person can do by himself or through his agent. Also, one’s property is called melakhah, as in whether he have not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods (melekhet) (Shemot 22:7). The word messenger (malakh) comes from the same root. A malakh (messenger) is so called because he is under the control of the one who sends him. The meaning of the word regel (the pace) is the same as le-ragli (because of me), as in and Hashem hath blessed thee because of me (le-ragli) (Bereshit 30:30). However, it is possible that le-regel should be taken literally, since Yaakov led the animals on foot.
[What needeth it?] I have no need of it.

And Yaakov came in peace. Shalem (peace) is an adjective. The meaning of our clause is, Yaakov came in peace to Shechem; i.e., no misfortune befell him on the way. Scripture notes this because it is about to tell of what happened to Dinah.

The parcel of ground. A portion in the field. Scripture mentions this to inform us of the greatness of the land of Yisrael. Whosoever has a portion in it is as though he had a portion in the world to come.

[And called it El-elohe-Israel.] Saadiah explained that and called it El-elohe-Israel means, He called to Hashem, “El-elohe-Israel.” However, the correct interpretation is that he called the altar El-elohe-Israel (Elokim, the Elokim of Yisrael). Moshe similarly called the altar he erected Adonai-nissi (Hashem is my banner) (Shemot 17:15) because of the miracle Elokim performed in that place. Similarly, when the Divine Presence will once again return to Yerushalayim, the city will be called Adonai-shammah (Hashem is there) (Yechezkel 48:35). Yaakov similarly called the altar whereupon he served Hashem, El-elohe-Israel (Elokim, the Elokim of Yisrael) because Elokim came to his aid. The name El (Elokim) means the One who is powerful and mighty.

Elohe-Israel. He saved him on the way and ensured his safe arrival in Kenaan, where Sukkot and Shechem are located. I believe that Yaakov spent many years in the city of Shechem, for at the time of Yaakov’s arrival in Shechem, Dinah was less than seven years old and also Shimon and Levi were yet small children.
And Dinah went out. Of her own accord.
And humbled her. He had normal intercourse with her. Scripture uses the term va-ye’anneha ( and humbled her) because she was a virgin.
And spoke comfortingly unto the damsel. He spoke tenderly and comfortingly to her.
That he had defiled. That Shechem had defiled.
A reproach. It will be a reproach for generations. This is the meaning of because he had wrought a vile deed in Yisrael (v. 7).

[13. And spoke because he had defiled.] And spoke to Shechem who had (asher) defiled their sister. We may interpret our verse in this manner because we find Scripture stating, dabbero le-shalom (Bereshit 37:4), which is to be rendered: speak peaceably unto him (Bereshit 37:4). On the other hand asher may mean because. In this case the Bible is telling us that they answered with guile because (asher) he had defiled Dinah their sister.

To one that is uncircumcised. One whose sexual member is uncircumcised. The meaning of the term orlah (uncircumcised) is something which is heavy. Aral (uncircumcised), in uncircumcised (aral) lips (Shemot 6:12), and arelah (dull), in their ear is dull (arelah) (Yirmiyahu 6:10), are similar. An orlah is something which lays heavy because it is an unnecessary appendage. Those who say that Avraham blemished himself by undergoing circumcision, and thereby violated Hashem’s charge to him, and be thou whole (Bereshit 17:1), err. The opposite is true. Proof of this can be offered from the animal kingdom. As to their query, why remove that which Hashem created, we respond that Hashem also created the umbilical cord.
Our daughter. They spoke thus because she was a minor. They referred to Dinah as our daughter because they spoke on behalf of Yaakov.

Deferred not. Echar (deferred) is not of the same grammatical form as va-echar (and stayed) in and stayed (va-echar) until now (Bereshit 32:5). Our word is a third person pi’el perfect following the paradigm of berakh (did curse) in Navot did curse (berakh) God and the King (Melachim I 21:13).
Peaceable. They are at peace.
Large enough. Yadayim (enough) is to be rendered places, as in Thou shalt have a place (yad) (Devarim 23:13).

Will the men consent. Ye’otu (consent) comes from the same root as ya’atah (befitteth) in For it befitteth (ya’atah) Thee (Yirmiyahu 10:7). The yod prefix is vocalized with a tzere to compensate for the missing first root letter.

Be circumcised. The word be-himmol (be circumcised) has already been explained. Shechem and Chamor had evil designs on Yaakov and his sons for they said, Shall not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours (v. 22)?

On the third day. The third day is always a difficult day because it is half of a monthly quarter. Shimon and Levi acted with the full consent of their brothers. This is clear from And the sons of Yaakov answered Shechem and Chamor his father with guile (v. 13). The “sons of Yaakov” refers to all of the brothers. Yaakov spilled his anger on Shimon and Levi because they killed the men of Shechem
Even all that was in the house. This refers either to the house of Shechem or Chamor.

Few in number. Mete (few) means men. Anything that can be numbered is deemed a few. Hence Rabbi Aharon Ha-Kohen, dean of the Yeshiva, errs in rendering literally vi-yehi metav mispar (in that his men became few) (Devarim 33:6).
To make me odious. They will hate me as one loathes something which gives off a horrible odor.
And they said. Shimon and Levi.
Should one deal with our sister as with a harlot. Should Shechem deal with our sister as with a harlot.

Put away the strange gods. Heaven forbid that the prophet would live with women who served strange gods. The explanation of this verse will be found in the Torah portion va-yelekh moshe (And Moshe went).
And purify yourselves. Wash your bodies.
And change your garments. From this verse we learn that a Yisraeli must have a clean body and spotless garments when he goes to pray in a place set aside for worship.
A terror of. The tav of chittat (terror of) receives a dagesh to compensate for the missing root letter, the tav.
[Because there Elokim was revealed to him.] Elokim (Elokim) refers to angels. Compare, And behold the angels of Elokim ascending and descending on it (Bereshit 28:12).
Thy name shall not be called anymore Yaakov. You shall no longer be called only Yaakov but also Yisrael.
Be fruitful and multiply. This is a blessing as in the account of the Creation.

[And Yaakov set up a pillar.] This may be a pluperfect meaning Yaakov had already set up a pillar. On the other hand, Yaakov may now have set up a pillar a second time. I prefer the first interpretation.

And he poured out a drink-offering thereon. He poured wine or water on the pillar. Yaakov first washed the pillar with wine or water and then poured oil thereon. Here at Beit El Yaakov kept his vow and gave a tithe of his wealth in honor of Hashem to a contemporary who was worthy to receive it.
Some way. It is possible that the caf of kivrat (some way) is a preposition meaning similar to and that brat is a distance measured by walking. The word does not appear elsewhere in Scripture.

When she was in hard labor. Be-hakshotah (when she was in hard) is a hifil. The meaning of be-hakshotah be-lidtah (when she was in hard labor) is: the delivery caused her pain. Va-tekash (and she had hard labor, in v. 16) is similar. However the latter is a pi’el. Va-tekash is similar to va-tekhal (and she was done) in And when she had done (va-tekhal) giving him drink (Bereshit 24:19).

Ben Oni. Ben Oni means the son of my mourning. Onim (mourners) in as the bread of mourners (onim) (Hoshea 9:4) and be-oni (my mourning) in I have not eaten thereof in my mourning (be-oni) (Devarim 26:14) are similar.
Her grave. Kevuratah (her grave) and kivrah (her grave) mean the same.
That Reuven went. Our sages explained this beautifully; for a prudent man concealeth shame (Mishlei 12:16).

That were born to him in Padan Aram. Actually only eleven sons were born to Yaakov in Padan Aram for Binyamin was born in the land of Kenaan. Scripture speaks of the majority of his sons. I will in the future point out many similar cases.

And Yitzchak expired. When Yitzchak died and was gathered to his people Easu and Yaakov buried him. Scripture mentions Esav before Yaakov because the Pentateuch follows the order of their birth. However, in relating the burial of Avraham the Bible reads, And Yitzchak and Yishmael his sons buried him (Bereshit 25:9) because Yishmael was the son of a handmaid.

The same is Edom. He is the father of Edom. Do not be surprised that Scripture here calls the daughter of Eilon the Chiti whom Esav married Adah, while earlier it refers to her by the name of Basmat (Bereshit 26:34), for she had two names. We find the same with the mother of Aviyah. Indeed, Aviyah himself (Divrei Hayamim II 11:20) is called Aviyam in the Book of Melachim (Melachim I 15:1) and Aviyah in Chronicles (Divrei Hayamim II 11:20). The Bible refers to them by two different names because both Aviyah and his mother had two names each.
These are the names of Esav’s sons (v. 10) refers to his grandchildren.

And Oholivamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tzivon the hivite. We find in our chapter a man called Anah who is the brother of Tzivon (v. 20). We further read that Tzivon had a son called Anah (v. 24). Our verse thus relates that Tzivon and his son Anah, or perhaps Tzivon and his brother Anah, slept with the same woman and the offspring did not know who their father was. However, it is also possible that Oholivamah was the daughter of Anah the son of Tzivon, and Scripture lists her as being the daughter of Anah and Tzivon in order to distinguish between Anah the son of Tzivon and Anah the brother of Tzivon. Some say that our chapter speaks of a Korach the son of Adah and Korach the son of Oholivamah. However, I believe that both are one and the same person. Korach was the son of Oholivamah. The reason he is listed among the chiefs of Elifaz is that he lived among them. It is also possible, since he was Oholivamah’s youngest son, that his mother died when he was still a child and that Adah raised him along with her own family and Scripture includes him with her children. Our case is similar to the five sons of Michal (Shmuel II 21:8). Korach thus became Adah’s son. Scripture similarly says that Amalek was a son of Adah because he was the son of the handmaid of her husband.

[Chief.] The meaning of alluf is a prince or chief. However, this is not the meaning of alluf (docile) in ke-kheves alluf (like a docile lamb) (Yirmiyahu 11:19). In the latter verse the caf prefixed to keves (lamb) also pertains to alluf; i.e., the verse is to be read as if written ke-kheves ke-alluf (like a lamb, like an ox). The latter is normal Hebrew usage, as can be seen in I went about as though it had been my friend (ke-re’a) or my brother (ke-ach) (Tehillim 35:14).

Seir. We do not know his pedigree. Scripture lists the children of Seir to inform us that they were of a different lineage from the children of Esav. The Bible notes this because Yisrael was prohibited from contending with the children of Esav.

The horite. Chori (Chori) means nobles. It is similar to chore (nobles) in the nobles (chore) of Yehudah (Yirmiyahu 27:20). It is possible that chori (Chori) comes from the same root as chorai in And they that weave cotton (chorai) (Is. 19:9), in which chorai means white stuff. Onkelos similarly renders white by chivvar. Nobles are called chorim (the white ones) because they are metaphorically speaking, like the color white, a color which resembles light. In contrast to chorim, mean men are called chashukkim (dark ones), as we read in He shall not stand before mean men (chashukkim) (Mishlei 22:29).
Ayah and Anah. The vav prefixed to Ayah has the same meaning as the Arabic fa. We have a similar clause without a vav prefixed to Ayah in Chronicles (Divrei Hayamim I 1:40).

The hot springs. Onkelos renders yemim (hot springs) mighty men as in The Eimim dwelt therein aforetime, a people great, and many, and tall (Devarim 2:10). It is possible to compare the two because we find the yod and alef interchanging as with the word yityammeru (bear themselves loftily) (Tehillim 94:4). However, Saadiah Gaon translates yemim as mules. He interprets who found to mean who crossbred. It is also possible that who found means who first discovered the technique of crossbreeding, since two different species cannot produce offspring. The latter interpretation is substantiated by Scripture’s stating, as he fed the asses of Tzivon his father. If the meaning of yemim is plants, as is maintained by many commentators, why should Scripture mention as he fed the asses of Tzivon his father?

And these are the children of Anah: dishon and Oholivamah the daughter of Anah. Anah the father of Oholivamah is not the same Anah mentioned in the first part of our verse, because if he is, there would be no need to mention him again. He is rather to be identified with the Anah mentioned in the preceding verse.

And these are the kings. Some say that this chapter records a prophecy. However, Yitzchaki claims in his book that this chapter was composed during the reign of King Yehoshafat. He explained the generations as he saw fit. Was he not rightly named Yitzchak? Everyone that heareth his interpretation will laugh at him. For he identified Hadar (v. 39) with Hadad the Edomi (Melachim I 11:14) and also said that Meheitavel (v. 39) is to be identified with the sister of Tachpeneis the queen of Mitzrayim. Far be it for one to believe that our chapter was written in the days of Yehoshafat as Yitzchaki maintains. Indeed his book is fit to be burned. Why did Yitzchaki maintain that it is impossible for eight Edomi kings to have reigned before Moshe when we find double the number of kings in Yisrael in about the same number of years? Furthermore, there were also proportionally many more kings of Yehudah in the same time period than the eight Edomi kings who reigned till the age of Moshe. The truth is that king, in before there reigned any king over the children of Yisrael, refers to Moshe who was king over Yisrael, and so it is written, And there was a king in Yeshurun (Devarim 33:5).

And Bela the son of Beor. Bela is not to be identified with Bilam the son of Beor, and neither is Baalam the son of Lavan the Arami. The Midrash which states that Baalam is the son of Lavan is probably based on the fact that both were sorcerers because “none of the words of our sages of blessed memory ever fall to the ground.” We cannot identify Baalam with Bela because Bela was an Edomi and Baalam an Arami. We are also not to identify Yovav the son of Zerach (v. 33) with Iyov, as Yitzchaki the windbag does.

Meheitavel the daughter of matred, the daughter of me-zahab. This is to be explained in the same manner as we interpret Oholivamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tzivon (v. 2). On the other hand Scripture may be listing Meheitavel’s mother and father.
Mei Zahav. This was his name. However, Saadiah Gaon says that Me-Zahab means a goldsmith. Others say Mei Zahav alludes to those who make gold out of copper. However, the latter is sheer nonsense.

[And these are the names of the chiefs that came of Esav…after their places] This means that their territories are well-known today (in the days of Moshe). These are the words of Moshe. Those now mentioned are the offspring of the chiefs mentioned above. Only those that had their own territories are mentioned.

Timna. Here it refers to a male. For we have many names which are used both for male and females. The same holds true for Oholivamah. It is also possible that the word chief is superfluous, the interpretation of the chief of Timna, the chief of Alvah, the chief Yetet being, the following are the chiefs of Timna, Elifaz’s concubine, Alvah and Yetet. Alvah and Yetet were chiefs of Amelek. There were seven chiefs of Oholivamah in the day of Moshe. Each of these chiefs had his own territory. Hence Moshe was explicit and added, according to their habitations.
And Yaakov dwelt. The Bible tells us that the chiefs of Esav dwelt on the mountain of Seir but that Yaakov dwelt in the chosen land.

The meaning of These are the generations of Yaakov is: these are the events which befell him and the incidents which came upon him. Toledot (generations) comes from the same root as yeled (bring forth) in What a day may bring forth (yeled) (Mishlei 27:1).

Being still a lad, even with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah. The sons of the concubines (the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah) made Yosef their attendant (servant) since he was their younger brother. This was the evil report of them which he brought unto their father. Had the children of Leah, the mistress of the house, made Yosef their attendant, then no wrong would have been done. The view that evil report pertains to limbs torn from living animals is a Midrashic interpretation. That Yosef did not bring an evil report to Yaakov concerning Leah’s children is clear from the fact that Scripture only mentions the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah in our verse.

Because he was the son of his old age. This is to be taken literally since Yosef was born to Yaakov when the latter was ninety-one years old. Also, Binyamin, his brother, is referred to by Scripture as a child of his old age (Bereshit 44:20). After Yosef and Binyamin no other children were born to Yaakov.
A coat of many colors. Ketonet passim means an embroidered coat.
[Many colors.] The word passim (many colors) is similar to the Aramaic word pas (part) in part of (pas) a hand (Daniel 5:5).
Speak unto him. Dabbero is to be rendered speak unto him.
[Peaceably.] Even peaceably.
Binding. Me’allemim (binding) comes from the same root as alummim (sheaves). The noun sheave is also found in the feminine, compare, bearing his sheaves (alummotav) (Tehillim 126:6).
Came round about. Tesubbenah (came round about) comes from a root whose second and third letters are identical. The bet receives a dagesh to compensate for a missing bet.
Shalt thou indeed reign over us? Or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? Shall we set thee up as a king over us? Or shalt thou rule over us by force.

And his father rebuked him. When the word ga’ar (rebuked) is followed by a bet it means to rebuke. When it is not followed by a bet it means to destroy. Compare, Behold, I will destroy (go’er) the seed for your hurt (Malachi 2:3). On the other hand, it is possible that the word go’er is used metaphorically in the aforementioned verse, its meaning being God will rebuke the seed and it will become frightened and not arise out of the ground.
I and thy mother. Thy mother refers to Bilhah his mother’s handmaiden who raised him.
Kept the saying. In his mind. This is also the correct meaning of kept in They kept His testimonies (Tehillim 99:7).
Here am I. I will do as you say.
And a certain man found him. According to the plain meaning of the text a passer by found him.
Where they are feeding the flock. If you know.
To dothan. Dotan is spelled both with and without a yod in our verse. In either case it refers to one and the same place.
They conspired. Va-yitnakkelu (they conspired) means they had evil designs. Nokhel (dealeth craftily) in But cursed be he that dealeth craftily (nokhel) (Malachi 1:14) is similar.

Let us not take his life. Our verse is similar to but his minister Yehoshua, the son of Nun, a young man (Shemot 33:11), the meaning of which is: but his minister Yehoshua, the son of Nun, did the ministry of a young man. The aforementioned verse must be so understood because Yehoshua was not at that time a young man. Similarly our verse should be read as if written: let us not strike him a mortal blow thus taking his life.

That they stripped. Va-yafshitu (that they stripped) is a causative. They told him to take the coat off by himself. Ketonet (coat) in Hebrew refers to a garment worn next to the skin. The brothers thus stripped Yosef of his garments and threw him naked into the pit.
And they sat down to eat bread. The nine brothers.
A caravan of Yishmeelim. Orechat is to be rendered caravan as Onkelos does. A caravan is so called because it travels on the roads (orechot).

Spicery. Rabbi Moshe Ha-Kohen the Spaniard explains nekhot (spicery) to mean a precious thing. Bet nekhoto (his treasure house) in and showed them all his treasure-house (bet nekhoto) (Melachim II 20:13) is similar. Nekhot and nekhoto are similar because the vav and the alef are interchangeable since they are quiescent letters.

And balm. The word for balm is encountered in Scripture vocalized with a quiescent sheva beneath the tzadi (utzri). We also find it vocalized with a chataf kamatz beneath the tzadi, viz., Is there no balm (ha-tzori) in Gilad? (Yirmiyahu 8:22). It also appears with the tzadi vocalized with a cholem, viz., and honey, and oil, and balm (ve-tzori) (Yechezkel 27:17). Saadiah Gaon explained that tzeri (balm) is a mixture of 75 roots. Others say that tzeri is a type of fruit. Still others say that it is either a fruit or the oil of a tree that, according to Yosef ben Gurion, was brought from Yericho to Mitzrayim. However, Rabbi Yishmael says that it means resin. We will rely on the latter opinion.
And ladanum. Saadiah Gaon says that lot (ladanum) is the same fruit that in Arabic is similarly called with the addition of a bet. Perhaps it is so.
What profit. Mah betza means what profit. Betza (profit) is close in meaning to chefetz (desire). What profit (betza) is there in my blood (Tehillim 30:10) is similar.
He is our brother our flesh. He is as our flesh since we all came from one flesh.

And there passed by. When the Yishmeeli merchantmen passed by them. Scripture refers to the Yishmeelim as Midyanim because the Midyanim are called Yishmeelim. The Book of Shoftim similarly says concerning the kings of Midyan, because they were Yishmeelim (Jud. 8:24).
And as for me, whither shall I go? Ani (I) is used twice in this clause even though one ani would have sufficed. The latter is in keeping with Hebrew style.

Without doubt torn in pieces. Toraf (torn) is a pu’al. The tet is vocalized with a cholam because it precedes a resh which cannot receive a dagesh. Morak (scoured) in it shall be scoured (u-morek), and rinsed in water (Vayikra 6:21) is similar.

And his father wept for him. Our sages interpreted this as referring to Yitzchak. The truth is that Yitzchak did not die until Yosef reached the age of twenty-nine. Some say that the prophetic spirit was removed from both Yaakov and Yitzchak because of their mourning. They offer proof from Elisha.
And all his daughters. His daughter and granddaughter.

[To the grave.] She’olah means down below, i.e., to the grave. Here the one who translated the Bible for those who err erred in translating she’olah as to hell. Proof of his mistranslation is, For the nether-world (she’ol) cannot praise Thee…They that go down into the pit cannot hope for Thy truth (Is. 38:18). Also in Tehillim 139:8, heaven is the antithesis of she’ol, viz., If I ascend up into heaven, Thou art there; If I make my bed in the nether-world (she’ol) behold Thou art there. Similarly Iyov states, The nether-world (she’ol) is naked before Him (Iyov 26:6). There are many other verses which prove that she’ol does not refer to hell.
The captain of the guard. The term tabbach (guard) is used both with reference to killing and with reference to cooking. Onkelos’ rendition is correct.

And it came to pass at that time. This does not refer to the time that Yosef was sold. It refers to the events that happened prior to that time. From thence they journeyed unto Gudgod…At that time Hashem separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of Hashem, to stand before Hashem to minister unto Him, and to bless in His name, unto this day (Devarim 10:7, 8) is similar. The tribe of Levi was chosen to minister unto Hashem in the second year while Yisrael journeyed to Gudgod in the fortieth year. I will explain the latter verses in their proper place. Why, then, did Scripture insert this chapter (Chap. 38) at this point when logic dictates that And Yosef was brought down to Mitzrayim (Bereshit 39:1) should follow And the Midyanim sold him (Yosef) into Mitzrayim (Bereshit 37:36)? The Bible placed this chapter (38) here to contrast the behavior of Yosef vis-a-vis his master’s wife with that of Yehudah toward his daughter-in-law. What forced me to offer this interpretation is the fact that only twenty-two years passed between the sale of Yosef and the descent of our ancestors into Mitzrayim. Now we learn in this chapter of the birth of Onan, Yehudah’s second son, and his reaching the age of procreation, which at the very earliest starts at the age of 12. Scripture goes on to state, And in the process of time (v. 12). The chapter then tells us that Tamar conceived and gave birth to Peretz. This same Peretz came to Mitzrayim with two sons of his own (Bereshit 46:12). Do not be disturbed by the question of Betzalel, for I will explain it when I come to it.

A certain Kenaani. Some say that kena’ani (Kenaani) means a merchant, as in As for the trafficker (kena’an), the balances of deceit are in his hand (Hoshea 12:8) and in, and in that day there shall be no more a trafficker (kena’ani) in the house of the Lord of Hosts (Zecharyah 14:21), wherein the word trafficker is spelled with a yod as in our verse. However, it is possible that the word kena’ani is to be taken literally. Our sages said, that Yehudah went down (v. 1) means that Yehudah was demoted from his leadership. However, this is a Midrashic interpretation. The Bible says that Yehudah went down because whoever goes from north to south is going down. Those acquainted with science will understand that what I say is correct.
At chezib. Keziv is the name of a place.

And perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her. This means, since you are her husband’s brother, show yourself to be a husband’s brother by going unto thy brother’s wife. I will expound a little on levirate marriage when I come to the portion, If brethren dwell together (Devarim 25:5), if Hashem prolongs my life till then.

That the seed would not be his. The seed would not be called by his name, as we find in And it shall be, that the first-born that she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother that is dead (Devarim 25:6).

That he spilled it on the ground. He destroyed the seed of his semen by pouring it outside of the vagina, on the ground. I am shocked by Ben Tamim Ha-Mizrachi who interpreted ve-shichet artzah (that he spilled it on the ground) to mean that Onan had unnatural intercourse with Tamar so that she would not conceive. Onan thus shichet artzah (corrupted her ground), i.e., the place upon which she sits on the ground. This interpretation is sheer madness. Heaven forbid that the holy seed become defiled with such filth.
Give seed. Neton (give) is here conjugated according to the paradigm of a regular verb.

Remain a widow in thy father’s house. The prepositional bet has been omitted from before the bet of the word house. We find the same type of omission in that was found in the house (bet) of Hashem (Melachim II 18:15).
And Yehudah was comforted. After Yehudah received condolences for his wife’s death he went up unto (al) his sheep shearers.
Al is to be understood as el (unto).
And covered herself. Ve-tekhas is a transitive verb. It means and covered herself.

And wrapped herself. The meaning of va-titallaf (she wrapped herself) is she hid her face. Va-yitallaf (Yonah 4:8) is similar. Its meaning is, Yonah hid his face in his garments. Similar in meaning both to our verse and Yonah (4:8) is the word me’ullefet (overlaid) in Overlaid (me’ullefet) with sapphires (Cant. 5:14).
In the entrance of enaim. Einayim is the name of a place. Others say that there were two springs with a door-like entrance on the road which Yehudah had to pass on his return to his home.

For she had covered her face. This explains the meaning of va-titallaf (and wrapped herself) (v. 14). Someone who explains for she had covered her face to mean that she covered her face with a variety of colored cosmetics and brought proof of this from his daughter is speaking nonsense, for one ought not to offer proof from fools. That which our sages say concerning Tamar’s chastity in her father-in-law’s house is also correct.

Thy signet. Because of Yehudah’s great lust he gave three objects as a pledge for something insignificant. I will explain the meaning of kedeshah (harlot) (v. 21) in my comments on There shall be no harlot (kedeshah) of the daughters of Yisrael, neither shall there be a sodomite (kadesh) of the sons of Yisrael (Devarim 23:18).
Let her take it. Forget about her and let her keep the pledge.
Lest we be put to shame. Lest I be a laughing stock, for giving a signet, cord and staff for something so insignificant.
[Behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.] This is a sign that she wants to keep the pledge.
About three months later. When one speaks of three months a mem is prefixed to the word three. When one speaks of three days a mem is suffixed to the word three.

When she was brought forth. If the alef of mutzet was not quiescent as is the grammatical rule, the word would have followed the paradigm of muda’at (made known) in This is made known (muda’at) (Is. 12:5).

Forasmuch as I gave her not. The expression ki al ken (for as much) has the same meaning as the Rabbinic term ho’il (since), as in forasmuch (ki al ken) as I have seen thy face (Bereshit 33:10). The meaning of our clause is: since I gave her not to Shelah my son. Or its meaning is, she did this because I gave her not to Shelah my son.
And he knew her again no more. He did not sleep with her again.

That one put out a hand. One of them put out a hand. The latter is not identified by name because he was not yet named. This birth, too, was out of the ordinary in that both placentas opened simultaneously and when this one drew back his hand, his brother came out.

Wherefore hast thou made a breach. Mah paratzta, alekhah paretz means, wherefore hast thou acted like a man who breaches a fence and goes through it. You are now responsible for the breach. Others say that paratzta is the same as u-faratzta (and thou shalt spread abroad) (Bereshit 28:14). Saadiah Gaon explains that paratzta is to be interpreted literally as meaning to make a breach but that paretz in alekhah paretz has the same meaning as va-yifrotz (it hath increased) in and hath increased (va-yifrotz) abundantly (Bereshit 30:30).

He knew not aught save the bread which he did eat. Some say that the bread which he did eat is a euphemism for a conjugal relationship. However, this interpretation is far-fetched. Furthermore, Potifar was a eunuch. I believe that what this verse says is that Potifar put Yosef in charge of everything that he had except for his bread, which Yosef was not permitted even to touch because he was a Hebrew, as we see from the verse because the Mitzrim might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Mitzrim (Bereshit 43:32). Potifar knew that Yosef was a Hebrew. Potifar’s wife similarly said, See, he hath brought in a Hebrew unto us to mock us (v. 14).
And Yosef was of beautiful form. Like his mother.
[To lie by her.] To just lie next to her, or to be with her, to converse with her.

And it came to pass on a certain day. On the same day that she had first asked him to lay with her. It was on this same day a week later, or a month later or a full year later. The latter appears correct to me.
To do his work. To supervise the housework or to oversee his master’s wealth, for Yosef was in charge of everything. The Midrash pertaining to and there was none of the men is an individual opinion.
He hath brought unto us. That is, my husband.
That his wrath was kindled. Potifar nevertheless did not kill Yosef because he wasn’t certain as to the truth of his wife’s accusation.

Prison. We can not ascertain whether bet ha-sohar (the prison) is a Hebrew or Mitzri word in view of the fact that the Bible goes on to explain its meaning as it does with the Parsi word ha-achashteranim (that were used in the King’s service) which is followed by the Hebrew bene ha-rammakhim (bred of the stud) (Est. 8:10).

And whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it. Some interpret this to mean that Yosef, like all the other prisoners, was engaged in work to support himself. However, I believe that the meaning of our verse is: and whatsoever they had to do there he was, as it were, the doer of it, because he was their supervisor. The next verse bears out the latter interpretation.
Offended. They committed an offense (chet) in a matter of state.

The fact that the samekh of sarisav (his officers) retains its kamatz is proof that the resh of saris (officer) should have received a dagesh, and since it cannot the samekh was vocalized with a long kamatz to compensate for the missing dagesh.
And he put them in ward in the house of the captain of the guard. A place where they would be guarded so they would not escape.

And the captain of the guard charged. When these two officers were put in a ward in the house of the captain of the guard, the latter remembered (pakad) Yosef; i.e., he recalled his abilities and brought him to his house and placed him in a dungeon which is the ward spoken of in our verse. The latter is the opinion of the great grammarian. However, I believe that the prison was in the house of the captain of the guard and Yosef was there to begin with. Proof of this is Scripture’s explicit statement, And he put them…into the prison, the place where Yosef was bound. What our verse relates is that the captain of the guard commanded (charged) Yosef to be with the butler and baker and serve them because they had high status in Paroh’s palace insomuch as they were officers of the king.

And they dreamed. The meaning of each man according to the interpretation of his dream is that each one of them saw in his dream details that could be interpreted to foretell what would happen in the future.
Sad. Zo’afim (sad) means agitated, as is the meaning of the word zapo (its rage) in and the sea ceased from its raging (mi-zapo) (Yonah 1:15).
And Yosef came in unto them. It is possible that Yosef used to sleep in the dungeon at night.

[Do not interpretations belong to Elokim.] Its meaning is that the interpretations of dreams belong to the Lord because He knows the future. He has revealed what is going to come to pass in a dream to one whom He selected and it therefore makes no difference whether I interpret the dream for good or ill. Since this is so, and all interpretations belong to Elokim, do not be concerned about telling me your dreams.
